articles.title: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York arrested for ‘engaging in prostitution’ and later charged with disorderly conduct
articles.summary: The principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers was arrested on Sunday and accused of “engaging in prostitution” in Ohio, according to court documents obtained by CNN.
articles.body: The principal owner of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers was arrested on Sunday and accused of “engaging in prostitution” in Ohio, according to court documents obtained by CNN. Jed York, who’s been with the team for nearly 20 years, became the chief executive officer in 2010. According to the court documents, York pleaded no contest to the charges of disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools after being detained in East Palestine. The documents state York paid $1,150 in fines associated with the charges and sentenced to a night in jail. CNN has reached out to the 49ers and York’s legal team for comment. NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said in a statement, “We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.” Columbiana County records show York had $160 seized and not returned to the team owner, but instead “forfeited” to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. The records also list that York completed an online course, though the specific nature of the course is not stated. The 46-year-old is the oldest son of Denise and John York, the co-chairmen of the 49ers. This story has been updated with additional reporting.

articles.title: WWE Contracts, '90-Day No-Compete Clause' Finally Explained by Former Champion in New Video
articles.summary: WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.
articles.body:
WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.

Raj Dhesi, formerly known as one-time WWE Champion Jinder Mahal, resurfaced his video explaining why wrestlers are required to sit out for 90 days after being cut, even though "there is no such thing as a no-compete clause in WWE."

"When you sign a WWE contract, in the writing it states, 'WWE can terminate your contract with 90 days' notice.' So when you receive the phone call, it's them letting you know that in 90 days, your contract is cut," Dhesi explained. "They will pay you for the 90 days. That distinction is very important, because if it was a no-compete clause, you would not get paid for 90 days. For 90 days, you are still under WWE contract."

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Dhesi went on to add that wrestlers who are cut are pulled from live events and shows to protect both themselves and the company from future liabilities such as injuries or misrepresenting the brand in any way.

"In my opinion, WWE paying you for 90 days is an incredible gesture," Dhesi said. "It gives you time to reorganize your life. You're not making moves out of desperation or anger, and it actually protects both parties."

articles.title: Panthers Expect RB Chuba Hubbard To Be Ready For Week 1
articles.summary: Panthers starting running back Chuba Hubbard injured his hamstring earlier in training camp.
articles.body: The Panthers' running back room is full of questions entering the 2026 season, but one of those has seemingly been answered. Coach Dave Canales said on Monday that the expectation is that injured back Chuba Hubbard will be ready for Week 1, per the Associated Press. Hubbard is expected to be the starting running back with Jonathon Brooks the second option, but a strained hamstring suffered during training camp has kept Hubbard from appearing in a single preseason game to this point. Due to that – and Hubbard not yet focusing on cutting due to the Panthers' caution, per Canales' own admission – the duo will work in a running back by committee approach to begin the year, per The Athletic.  A calf injury limited Hubbard in 2025, which cost him starts in favor of Rico Dowdle: Hubbard appeared in 15 games but started just the first six, and went from averaging 13.2 attempts and 47 yards per game to 6.1 rushes and 25.4 yards per over his last nine appearances. A second-round pick in 2024, Brooks appeared in just three games as a rookie before the 21-year-old suffered a second torn ACL and missed the rest of that season and the subsequent one recovering. Now healthy, he is listed as the second back on the Panthers' depth chart, ahead of Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyrus III, though, Brooks has just eight carries so far this preseason. In 2024, his last healthy season, Hubbard had 250 rushing attempts for 1,195 yards and 10 touchdowns in 15 games, all starts. articles.title: Ex-Liverpool star Fabinho reunited with Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023, where he won the league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.
articles.body:
Brazil ⁠midfielder Fabinho has ⁠signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor, the Turkish Super Lig football side has announced, and will link up with ⁠former Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah .

The 32-year-old midfielder will receive a 2.6-million-euro ($3.03m) guaranteed fee and a 1.4-million-euro ($1.63m) signing ⁠fee per season, according to a Turkish stock exchange filing made by the team on Monday.

“An agreement has been reached for a two-year contract with … Fabinho, who is currently in free status,” Trabzonspor posted on ‌X.

Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023 and helped the team win the domestic league after his five-year stint at Liverpool.

“A really special feeling to be playing with Salah again … I had the opportunity to play with him for five years in Liverpool. He is a person whom I respect a lot both for ⁠what he has done and what he ⁠will do,” Fabinho said after arriving at Trabzon airport earlier on Monday.

Looking to reignite his chemistry with 34-year-old Salah, Fabinho said: “I will always try to do the ⁠best I can with whatever ability I have.

“Along with the experience and leadership that come from ⁠playing for so many years, I will ⁠always try to help my teammates.”

Fabinho made 219 appearances for Liverpool, helping it win the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, League Cup, Club World Cup and UEFA Super Cup ‌titles.

Egypt forward Salah joined Trabzonspor as a free agent earlier this month.

Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish top flight last season, and take on Hungary’s Ferencvaros on Thursday in the second leg of their Europa League playoff tie, trailing 1-0.

articles.title: 'An unfortunate racket': As India nears its 100th chess Grandmaster, is an expensive coach all you need?
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: In 1978, the chess world was a reflection of a fiercely guarded aristocracy, it can be said. The title of Grandmaster (GM) was not merely a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In 1978, the chess world was a reflection of a fiercely guarded aristocracy, it can be said. The title of Grandmaster (GM) was not merely a designation. Rather, it was an exclusive fraternity reserved for the absolute statistical anomalies of the human race.To understand what has happened to the modern chess ecosystem, one must first understand what a Grandmaster used to be. To many historians, the very definition of chess mastery has been fundamentally altered."A Grandmaster result has been a performance equivalent to a 2600 rating. In 1978, there were only six players above 2600. And in 1981, I think there were about twelve or thirteen. So a 2600 performance essentially boiled down to doing as well as the top six or seven or ten players in the world," India's veteran Grandmaster Pravin Thipsay told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction.The rating inflation over the ensuing decades has been astronomical. Thipsay believes a 2600 rating in the early 1980s was the equivalent of a 2750 rating today, a tier reserved exclusively for the absolute best in the business today.Yet, the threshold to earn the GM title remains anchored to the 2600 performance. "Which means the International Master (IM) norm in the 1980s or in the '70s was more difficult than today's Grandmaster title," Thipsay added with a smile.Many feel it has not been an organic evolution of the sport but a deliberate, commercial policy choice.Between 1914 and 1997, the world produced fewer than 300 Grandmasters. But in 1998, under the leadership of then-FIDE President Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, the governing body prioritised global expansion. The criteria for titles were relaxed, and the rating floor, once a jaw-dropping mark of 2200, was eventually plummeted to 1000 (before settling at 1400 more recently in 2024).By 2004, the world had 1,000 Grandmasters. Today, there are over 2,500."FIDE started collecting fees for rated players," Thipsay noted, outlining the financial incentive behind the dilution. "It became an important way of getting money for FIDE during Kirsan's time. He specifically made it clear in the Congress in 1998 and 2000 that we want to lower down the title, we want to lower down the rating. He said, 'We want to make everything easy for you so that you can find sponsors more easily.'"The Indian explosionAgainst this backdrop of global title inflation, India stands on the precipice of a historic milestone.In a matter of weeks, if not days, the nation will crown its 100th Grandmaster. It is a sumptuous achievement for a country that waited until 1988 for Viswanathan Anand to become its first.Today, India is an undeniable superpower as it keeps on churning out prodigies who casually dismantle the worldâs elite.But beneath the glittering surface of this golden generation lies a complex, often unspoken reality.As FIDE titles and ratings became vastly more accessible, the grassroots culture of the sport underwent a radical, heavily commercialised shift. The gritty, egalitarian days of the game have gradually evaporated, replaced by an ecosystem catered strictly to the affluent."There were tournaments where everybody played, everybody stayed in a dormitory, and 80%, 90% of the money collected would go for the prize money," Thipsay recalled. "Organisers like YMCA provided halls and dormitory accommodation free, and people didn't really bother. I remember 40, 50 people staying together for my National Juniors, and nobody really grumbled about it."Today, things are different. One-day rapid tournaments routinely charge entry fees of Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000. Organisers rake in lakhs, while prize funds remain disproportionately small."By keeping such high entry fee, you have actually ended up making it a sport for rich people," Thipsay argued. "A common man, a child of a clerk or a laborer is not able to play even a one-day tournament irrespective of the prize. The entire chess-playing crowd has become the elite class who can afford such luxurious tournaments."The "complacency in mediocrity"Because FIDE ratings are now easily obtained, a dangerous phenomenon has taken root in Indian society. It is what Thipsay terms "complacency in mediocrity".Getting a rating today is, in his words, "probably one of the easiest things", achievable by a child after just a year of play. Yet, parents treat it as a monumental triumph.Drunk on early, low-level success, families make drastic life decisions. "Parents think, and the players think that they are good players; they are going to become Grandmasters very soon," Thipsay said."Grandmaster is everybody's ambition, whereas I think the title has not been lowered down to that level that everybody can become Grandmaster. Needless to say, there are many players who give up their studies and try their best in playing, and they end up remaining at the rating level of 1500 to 1700. Most of the players who played chess for thousands of hours, not going to school, remain between 1500 to 1800 level. And now they already have a bad academic record."With limited professional options outside the sport, these stalled players pivot to the only available avenue, which is coaching.This massive supply of trainers has birthed a sprawling, unregulated industry. Parents are liquidating assets and funnelling lakhs of rupees into private coaching, convinced it is the only path to the GM title."A need for coaching does not exist, but it is created," Thipsay, a renowned coach himself, remarked. "The way the coaching takes place is basically spoon-feeding rather than teaching chess."The doctrines of the legends like Dr Emanuel Lasker and Garry Kasparov, who preached that chess cannot merely be taught, tell us that the sole duty of a coach is to cultivate independent thinking."If you see, out of one lakh players, only three or four are able to think independently," Thipsay told this website. "We often have to de-train students for two to three years. An untrained child is much easier to teach than a trained child who is often on a wrong track."Further stressing the notion of independent thinking, he added, "Itâs very easy to become a Grandmaster if there is group discussion, if players come together, meet and discuss among themselves. All they need is the process of independent thinking. We need a coach who coaches, say, for 10 hours and teaches them to think independently."You will not have everybody becoming a Grandmaster. But many of the International Masters in the country would probably have become Grandmasters even without coaching, if they had decided to sit down together and analyse. Many of them may already be doing that as well."Itâs very easy to become a Grandmaster if there is group discussion, if players come together, meet and discuss among themselves.Nevertheless, the ongoing chess boom has perpetuated the general idea that an aspiring player must spend a heavy amount on elite coaching to reach the pinnacle."It's only a myth, and it's created to promote the coaches," Thipsay said, pointing out that players like R Praggnanandhaa, D Gukesh, and Aravindh Chithambaram became top-level Grandmasters without spending exorbitant sums on coaching early on.Furthermore, the financial return on investment is bleak.The veteran GM revealed, "The average income of an Indian Grandmaster through winnings in chess tournaments is less than one and a half lakhs per year. It's something I would call an unfortunate racket rather than expensive coaching."The pure talent argumentIs Thipsay right? Is the modern coaching industrial complex entirely a racket?Grandmaster Aravindh Chithambaram, a multiple-time National Champion known for his immense natural talent and humble beginnings, pushes back slightly on the idea that exorbitant wealth is a prerequisite, but he acknowledges the steep climb."Not necessarily I feel like one can become a Grandmaster only if he spends 20 lakhs or 30 lakhs," Aravindh told TimesofIndia.com."I think if a person is really skillful, he can achieve no matter what. But of course, the initial stages would be very hard. Because if you're not a Grandmaster or even an International Master, of course you will have to spend a lot of money. But once you make the first step, I think the rest of them would be easier comparatively. The first step would be very hard, I would say. But once you understand that you are skillful, you have the talent playing, then things are much easier."For players of Aravindh's calibre, raw skill eventually attracts sponsors, mitigating the financial burden.But for those who don't possess generation-defining talent, the necessity of a coach is less about "spoon-feeding" and more about an invaluable, finite resource like time.The pragmatic truth of the "Engine Era"Delhi's Aaryan Varshney, who recently became Indiaâs 92nd Grandmaster, offers a compelling counterweight to Thipsayâs purist philosophy.Varshneyâs journey is highly unusual. He reached the GM title at 21 without a formal academy, expensive foreign trainers, or a titled coach.Instead, he was guided entirely by his father, Gaurav, a single parent who left his job to study the game alongside his son. Yet, despite his DIY success story, Varshney is adamant that going it completely alone in the modern era is a mistake."If someone really wants to become GM, then they have to have someone who can sit with them and analyse games, sometimes all night, like my father did," Varshney told this website."A coach wouldn't necessarily do as much as my father did. But you need someone, at the very least. You can't do everything completely on your own. I didn't do anything. I'm telling you from my own experience. My father did the whole thing for me. So, doing everything yourself makes the journey difficult. You need a coach."If you're doing something yourself, something that might take us five hours, a coach can get you to do it in one hour.To Varshney, the value of a coach is not in inflating a player's ego, but in condensing the gruelling hours of modern computer engine analysis."It's not necessary for your coach to be an IM or a GM. The important thing is that the coach should be good, someone who can actually teach the child," Varshney pointed out. "If you're doing something yourself, something that might take us five hours, a coach can get you to do it in one hour. Would you rather spend five hours or one hour? Obviously, everyone would prefer one hour."Varshney's reality check underlines the modern burden placed on young players."Even analysing games yourself becomes difficult, because when you look at the engine, you can get stuck trying to understand why a particular move is good," Varshney explained. "Someone who already has that knowledge can explain it to you easily. Whatever I was struggling to understand, my father would explain it to me in two minutes. Otherwise, I would just sit there trying to figure it out."As India approaches its 100th Grandmaster, the ecosystem supporting these players remains a paradox.Thipsay is undeniably right. The title is statistically easier to obtain than it was in 1978, and the fear-mongering that demands parents spend lakhs on coaching is, in many cases, a predatory racket preying on affluent families.Yet, Varshneyâs lived experience proves that in the modern computer era, navigating the labyrinth of chess theory without a guide is a punishing task.Also Read: Gave up IIT, left home, slept on roads: How Rajasthan's first AGM put Udaipur on global chess mapA player does not need an exorbitant, six-figure coaching setup to become a Grandmaster. But they do need a translator for the digital age.India will soon celebrate its 100th Grandmaster. But behind the celebratory headlines, the true challenge will remain as to how the ecosystem ensures the sport remains a battle of minds, rather than a battle of bank accounts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Texans Reportedly Acquire WR Kayshon Boutte From Patriots For S Jaylen Reed
articles.summary: The Houston Texans reportedly acquired wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots on Monday in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick.
articles.body: The Houston Texans are adding much-needed depth at wide receiver.  Houston has agreed to a deal to acquire wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick, The Ringer reported on Monday.  The draft selection sent to New England originally belonged to the New Orleans Saints, according to NFL Network. The trade addresses an immediate roster need for Houston following a season-ending knee injury to wide receiver Jayden Higgins during last week's joint practice session with the Las Vegas Raiders. Higgins was expected to hold a starting role in the Houston offense before suffering a torn ACL. Boutte spent his first three seasons with New England after being selected in the 2023 draft. Last season, the receiver recorded 33 receptions for 551 yards and six touchdowns in a bit of a breakout year. However, Boutte became expendable this offseason following the Patriots' moves at wide receiver. They made a big trade for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs to a pricey contract. Brown and Doubs joined a wide receiver room that also features DeMario "Pop" Douglas, Kyle Williams and Mack Hollins.  So, Boutte's name emerged in trade rumors over the offseason and into training camp. He addressed the trade speculation during training camp last week. "I'm just blocking out the noise. That's the main thing. We all hear the stuff that's going on," Boutte told reporters. "But like I always said, I'm where I'm at. My feet are here, so I'm not worried about what's next or what's behind me. Just being present." In return, New England acquires Reed to bolster their secondary along with future draft compensation. Boutte now joins a Houston receiving group that features Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, and Tank Dell. articles.title: Mike McCarthy Admits Steelers, CB Joey Porter Jr. Remain At 'Impasse' Over New Deal
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy wants to work with Joey Porter Jr., but the Pittsburgh Steelers and the cornerback are at an impasse over a new deal.
articles.body: Mike McCarthy wants the chance to work with Joey Porter Jr. When McCarthy gets that chance is anyone's guess, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach included. McCarthy said Monday that the club and the fourth-year cornerback are at an impasse as the two sides try to work out a new deal. The Steelers placed Porter on the physically unable to perform list when training camp opened with what the team described as a back issue that flared up during a mobility test. It seems Porter's back problems are just part of the reason he has yet to take the practice field with the season opener against Atlanta less than three weeks away. "I learned this in my early years as a head coach, you have to separate the business from the football," McCarthy said. "Sometimes it’s easier than others." Porter is in the final season of the four-year deal he signed after the Steelers selected him with the first pick of the second round in 2023. While Pittsburgh has locked up other members of that draft class — including outside linebacker Nick Herbig and tight end Darnell Washington — Porter's status seems a little more uncertain. The 26-year-old is coming off his best season as a pro, and he said during minicamp in June that he long felt he's one of the top players at his position and that he believes he will be paid that way. The top of the cornerback market has been particularly hot of late, with Seattle’s Devon Witherspoon agreeing to a massive new deal and New England’s Christian Gonzalez getting offered one in recent weeks. Though Porter, who has three interceptions across three seasons, might not be in that neighborhood yet, he also might not be far off. Though he has deep ties to Pittsburgh — he grew up in the city while his father, Joey Porter Sr., played and then later coached for the Steelers — he didn't rush to sign his rookie deal in 2023, waiting until the eve of training camp to do it. Porter essentially "held in" during minicamp, participating in individual drills but staying out of full 11-on-11 work, a not uncommon tactic by players seeking new contracts. McCarthy described the situation as a challenge, in part because the entirety of Pittsburgh's defensive staff is in its first season. "Every one of us has a contract," McCarthy said. "The organization, they have beliefs and so forth. So that's where we are." While Porter remains out, veteran defensive back Jalen Ramsey and rookie first-round offensive tackle Max Iheanachor returned to practice on Monday. Ramsey has been on the PUP list since the start of camp because of a knee injury sustained during minicamp in June. The eight-time Pro Bowler said the defense is still getting up to speed and it's important for the entire secondary to be available when the Falcons visit on Sept. 13. "They need to pay Joey Porter," Ramsey said. Iheanachor, taken 21st overall in the draft, hadn't practiced since hurting his upper body on Aug. 6. McCarthy didn't rule out Iheanachor making an appearance when Pittsburgh wraps up the preseason on Thursday night in Buffalo. "We got two padded practices (this week), so it’ll be a really good indication of how much he’ll be able to play personally," McCarthy said. "We'll see how it goes." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Former NBA players not eligible for WNBA, sources say
articles.summary: Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to play in the WNBA, sources around the league confirm.
articles.body: Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to play in the WNBA, sources around the league told CNN on Monday. ESPN was first to report on the news. Both men announced last month that they now identify as women and said they planned to enter the 2027 WNBA draft amid a national conversation surrounding gender eligibility policies and transgender inclusion in women’s sports. However, no transgender women have played in the WNBA. The sources firmly rejected the draft declarations, characterizing them as publicity stunts designed to mock the league, sow division, and draw attention to the topic by demeaning others. There are no legitimate or immediate eligibility matters requiring action by the WNBA at this time, the sources said. The league has said it plans to approach the broader topic “thoughtfully” alongside its primary stakeholders, including players, teams and the union, and would not allow “outside pressure or manufactured controversy to dictate” its internal processes or force a response to efforts intended to demean others. On Sunday, Freedom was ejected after a high-profile courtside incident at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. During the third quarter of the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky game, Freedom, who was seated along the baseline wearing a shirt bearing the definition of a woman, got into a heated verbal exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. “It’s always women hating on other women,” Freedom posted on X after the game. No formal announcement or disciplinary ruling regarding a potential game ban for Freedom has been made.

Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 24. Scroll down for updates of all the action from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

OTM put Jimmy through the announce table while Keys held Jey and forced him to watch. The show ended with Knight, Solo and The Usos all down around the ring as OTM and Keys stood tall in the ring.

The Usos still had the upper hand all through the break into the next segment. They kept Sikoa isolated with quick tags and double-team moves.

The Street Champ hit a desperate clothesline to give himself some breathing room. Knight and Jimmy both tagged in at the same time. The Megastar unloaded on the elder Uso with jabs and a clothesline.

As Jey and Solo were fighting at ringside, Royce Keys put both of them through the barricade with a huge Spear. In the ring, OTM from NXT attacked Knight and Big Jim.

Bronco Nima and Lucien Price helped Keys destroy all four men. It looks like we officially have a new trio on Raw to compete with The Bloodline.

The Usos vs. LA Knight and Solo Sikoa Part 1

Jimmy and LA came out of the gate hot as soon as the bell rang. Knight hit a clothesline to get the first takedown before tagging in Solo for a double back elbow.

The Usos were able to take control with some combined attacks. They took Solo out of the ring and drilled him with a double superkick.

After a video hyping Zilla Fatu in NXT, Chad Gable was talking to Pearce backstage, and the GM said he is going to go find a new challenger for him. Ethan Page walked up and congratulated him on winning the IC title from Rey Mysterio.

All Ego said Gable is intimidated by him, but Gable reminded him that he beat him to earn the title shot in the first place. He said he would have given Page a title shot, but the way he is acting has made him change his mind.

Back in the arena, The Usos came out for their match against Sikoa and Knight.

Penta had control through the break, but the living skeleton started to regain his footing. He took Penta down with a few high-flying moves and scored a two-count with a powerslam.

La Parka drilled the former IC champion with a DDT for a close two-count. Penta caught him with a Penta Driver, but he couldn't keep him down for the pin.

A Spanish Fly got La Parka another near-fall before Penta wrenched his arm behind his back. He hit the Mexican Destroyer to seal the victory and advance to the finals.

This was a solid match, but the most intriguing part of this is that we will see Penta and Fenix fight in the finals next week to determine who gets to face Roman Reigns for the world title in Mexico City.

Lyra Valkyria had a brief exchange with Sol Ruca and Iyo Sky before Penta made his way out first to take on La Parka in the other semifinal match in the ongoing No. 1 Contender's tournament.

The luchadores started with a fast-paced exchange, but Penta took control. He sent La Parka out of the ring so he could take him down with a dive through the ropes.

La Parka recovered and hit a moonsault from the middle rope to the floor. Penta caught him with a superkick as he was coming off the top rope, but it only got him a two-count.

We returned to see Cass missing a corner splash. Evans tried to build a little momentum, but he couldn't take Cass off his feet. The big man caught him, but Evans sent him over the top rope before hitting a suicide dive.

The Young OG put Cass in the timekeeper's area so he could hit a running dive over the barricade. Evans started unloading on him with punches and kicks.

He brought Cass back in the ring and hit the Red Dot kick and a springboard clothesline. He went for the OG Cutter, but Cass shoved him off the top turnbuckle.

He nailed Je'Von with a big boot for the win. This seemed like a pretty abrupt ending, and an odd choice for a finishing move.

Judgment Day attacked Evans after Cass left the ring and left him down and out.

Big Cass has been making Evans' life hard recently, so they met in what was the first match Cass has had in WWE since returning. The way they shot the entrance for Cass was designed to make him look as big as possible, and it worked.

Evans tried to stick and move to avoid the big man. He brought the powerhouse out of the ring with a hurricanrana, but when he went for a slingshot crossbody, Cass caught him. Je'Von got back in the ring and Cass leveled him with a clothesline over the top rope.

Michael Cole talked about the journey Cass has been on since he was fired by WWE eight years ago as we saw him throw Evans into the barricade. He said Cass has taken no accountability for his actions.

Paul Heyman and Adam Pearce were in the ring for a contract signing between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker. The Ruler made his entrance first as the crowd chanted his name.

Breakker asked Femi who he thinks he is, claiming to be the future. He asked what Femi has done to earn the title of being the future of WWE. He diminished Femi's King of the Ring win and victory over Brock Lesnar.

He talked a lot of trash about how Femi wouldn't even be where he is if Breakker hadn't been out with an injury for months. The Ruler called him an angry, orange man and said he can't understand that his chances of being the face of WWE are gone.

Breakker signed the contract and said Femi is going to realize he is the one guy he can't beat. He taunted Oba by saying Heyman should sign it for him since they are so close now.

Bron and Oba ended up brawling after Breakker threatened Heyman. Austin Theory showed up to help his partner, but Femi fought them off and put Theory through the table.

We returned to see both men trading chops. Lee hit a few kicks to take Fenix off his feet. He hit a beautiful float over into a powerbomb, but it couldn't get him the win.

They continued to trade fast-paced offense until they ended up fighting near the announce table. Fenix was tripped on the table, which gave Lee an opening to hit a massive cannonball through the second rope that hit Fenix off the top of the table.

That spot was wild! The crowd chanted "This is awesome" as Lee brought Fenix in for a tornado DDT to get a two-count. Rey hit a brainbuster as he began regaining momentum.

He got Lee up for the Mexican Muscle Buster, but Lee countered into the Styles Clash for a near-fall. They kept going back and forth until Fenix finally hit his finisher to get the win.

This match was incredible. If you are not watching the show live, make sure you check this one out. Both guys worked their butts off to make this awesome.

The No. 1 Contender's tournament continued this week with Rey Fenix taking on Dragon Lee in the semifinals. Before the match, Je'Von Evans attacked Dom Mysterio and JD McDonagh backstage, which Rey Mysterio seemed to love.

They started with a quick exchange of holds and counters. Neither man could get an advantage as they went move for move. They came to a stalemate before they began trading strikes.

Lee was the first one to take control with a nice dropkick in the corner for a two-count, but Fenix wasn't down for long. He hit the running kick across the top rope he is known for, and he followed it with a diving crossbody for a near-fall.

The AAA cruiserweight champion hit a moonsault on the floor, but when they got back into the ring, Lee hit a German suplex. He took Fenix down with a huge dive over the top rope that sent us into the break.

Perez had control through the break, but Vaquer was starting to make a comeback when we returned. Roxy had to pull her hair to escape an abdominal stretch, but the former world champion maintained control.

She used the Devil's Kiss to slam Roxanne's head into the mat 10 times. She used a brutal dragon screw leg whip in the corner before hitting a running double knee against the turnbuckle.

Perez recovered and hit a nice shining wizard for a two-count. Stephanie countered a crossface into a package backbreaker. Morgan interfered while Rodriguez distracted the ref. This brought out Becky Lynch.

Roxy tried to take advantage of all the mayhem, but Vaquer was able to hit her with her finisher to score the win.

Lynch took Morgan out at ringside before getting into the ring. She and Vaquer exchanged a few words before The Man made her exit.

Stephanie Vaquer vs. Roxanne Perez Part 1

Stephanie Vaquer returned to action for the first time since WrestleMania to take on Roxanne Perez. La Primera made her way to the ring right before the break. Liv Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez were at ringside.

Perez played some mind games by avoiding Vaquer a few times before slapping her and then hiding in the ropes. Once Vaquer got her hands on her, she wrestled her to the mat and stomped on her elbow.

Roxy fooled her into chasing her back into the ring. They traded stiff slaps before Stephanie almost locked her in an armbar. Vaquer hit a running kick in the corner, but a distraction from Raquel allowed Perez to shove her off the top rope.

LA Knight came to the ring to kick things off with a promo. He said he needs to talk about the coward, Roman Reigns.

He talked about Reigns refusing to defend the belt against him and how he wasn't able to compete in the current tournament going on with AAA.

Solo Sikoa appeared in the crowd and used Knight's own catchphrase before thanking him for helping out last week with The Bloodline. A moment later, The Usos started making their way to the ring.

When Jey sent him a warning shot, Solo pretended like he was in The Matrix to avoid it. They ended up agreeing to a tag match with the four of them for later in the show.

Knight and Sikoa are so great together. They are always funny whenever they interact.

Monday Night Raw is officially on the air. This week's episode had an early start time due to a double taping alongside SmackDown.

Shots of various Superstars backstage were shown before we went to a video recapping what happened last week with The Bloodline.

articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From Aug. 24
articles.summary: WWE rolled into the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa for the August 24 episode of Raw, headlined by a contract signing featuring Oba Femi and Bron Breakker.
articles.body:
WWE rolled into the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa for the August 24 episode of Raw, headlined by a contract signing featuring Oba Femi and Bron Breakker.

What went down when they shared the same ring in a highly combustible situation?

Find out in this recap of Monday's show, including grades and analysis for the night's No. 1 contender's tournament match-ups.

Announced in advance of Monday's show were:

No. 1 Contender's Tournament Match: Rey Fenix vs. Dragon Lee

No. 1 Contender's Tournament Match: Penta vs. La Parka

Oba Femi and Bron Breakker contract signing

Last Time In Action: LA Knight, Solo Sikoa, and Royce Keys defeated The Bloodline (SummerSlam, August 1)

LA Knight and Solo Sikoa sent a warning shot to The Bloodline after dropping Roman Reigns and The Usos last week, kicking off the show with an in-ring promo that perfectly blended humor and serious, story-advancing work.

Interrupted by Jimmy and Jey Uso, though, the united duo accepted a challenge for a main event match later in the show and got the last word, to the delight of the fans.

A solid segment that showcased Sikoa's enormous personality, this was a great follow-up to last week's show-closing segment, on a night when the OTC is not scheduled to appear.

Sikoa was genuinely funny here. His impersonation of Knight was outstanding and his Matrix reaction to Jey's "warning shot" was right out of Scary Movie . He's going to become a huge babyface star for WWE.

Knight is doing some of his best work right now. He seems motivated by his spot, a spot that should have been his far sooner than it is.

Last Time in Action: Stephanie Vaquer lost to Liv Morgan (WrestleMania, April 18); Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez lost to Iyo Sky and Sol Ruca (Raw, August 10)

Stephanie Vaquer scored her first victory in her first match in four months, defeating The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez in singles competition on Monday.

The Prodigy put up a tough fight, working over La Primera, who showed some signs of ring rust but shook it off for the most part down the stretch.

Overcoming interference from Women's World Champion Liv Morgan and Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez, Vaquer downed Perez, thanks to the arrival of Becky Lynch, and earned the win to continue building momentum toward a championship opportunity.

After the match, Lynch and Vaquer exchanged words, keeping the tension between them alive in what is becoming one of the best programs on the Raw brand.

Perez is almost wasted in this role. The issues between her and Morgan are nearly non-existent at this point. She has largely become the tackling dummy for the Judgment Day, working matches and losing them as part of everyone else's story. One of the best wrestlers in the company, hopefully that trend changes sooner rather than later.

Vaquer looked good in her first match in four months. She looked a tad slower, but that ring rust will be erased the more ring time she gets in the coming weeks and months.

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee defeated El Hijo del Dr. Wagner Jr. (Raw, August 17); Rey Fenix defeated El Fiscal (Raw, August 17)

Two of the best luchadors in professional wrestling squared off in the semifinals of the No. 1 Contender's Tournament, a chance to challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship on September 14 in Mexico City, on the line, as AAA Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix battled Dragon Lee.

Chants of "this is awesome" rained from the stands as Lee launched himself through the ropes with a tope suicida and wiped Fenix out on the announce table. Back in the ring, he delivered a big DDT for two.

Fenix delivered a rolling cutter to a charging Lee, then added the Mexican Muscle Buster for the pinfall victory to cash his ticket to the finals of the tournament.

This was an excellent match that highlighted two woefully underutilized talents. Fans in Montreal were red hot for everything they did, and the result was an enhanced experience that proved that sometimes the best thing WWE can do to win over the audience is to let two extraordinary in-ring talents deliver between the ropes.

How many times does Lee have to show up and show out before enjoying a sustained push?

Are we really going to get a Fenix vs. Penta match before we ever see them team up as the Lucha Bros? It certainly looks that way.

Oba Femi and Bron Breakker Sign on the Dotted Line

Last Time In Action: Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar (SummerSlam, August 1); Bron Breakker defeated Joe Hendry (Raw, August 3)

Ahead of their showdown on September 6 at Sunday Night's Main Event, Oba Femi and World Tag Team Champion Bron Breakker met in the squared circle to sign the contract for their encounter.

Femi told Breakker that if he debuted in 2002 or 2014, he would have been the future of the industry. Unfortunately, he came around in 2026 and has the unenviable task of encountering The Ruler.

Breakker claimed that he would prove that he is the one guy Femi cannot beat.

The heel continued the narrative that Paul Heyman may be more closely aligned to Femi, angrily demanding the advocate sign for The Ruler.

He used that distraction as an opportunity to deliver a cheap shot before Austin Theory arrived on the scene. A two-on-one beatdown ensued before Femi powered out, sent Breakker to the floor, and drove his tag team partner through the table.

This was a strong segment, with Femi shining on the mic. To borrow a phrase used more frequently on WWE TV, he dog-walked Breakker, outshining him on the mic. He looked confident and comfortable while his opponent on SNME stumbled once or twice while cutting a more generic promo.

Femi referenced Roman Reigns, saying that Breakker would have been the future guy had he debuted in 2014 and gone up against "whoever the 'big dog' was at that time." Oh yeah...that match is going to slap when it finally happens.

Just in case you did not know what Theory's role was in the Vision, him going through the table as an afterthought was should have confirmed it for you.

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans defeated JD McDonagh (Raw, August 17); Big Cass lost to Daniel Bryan (Money in the Bank, June 17, 2018)

Big Cass wrestled his first match in eight years, battling Je'Von Evans and potentially biting off more than he could chew.

His size and strength advantage was negated at times by The Young OG's speed and creativity, and he was forced to fight from underneath late in the match-up.

The NXT export caught Evans, knocked him from the top rope to the ring apron, and rocked him with a big boot to the face to score the win, his lip busted and bloodied as evidence of the grueling competition he had just endured.

Booking Cass to go 50-50 with Evans was certainly a choice considering he just made his return, but The Young OG is not someone you want getting run over at this point in his career, either.

Considering the corner WWE Creative booked itself into, this was a fine match that highlighted both men and gave Cass a strong victory.

After the match, Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh attacked, hinting at the next program for Evans.

Cass looked great for a guy wrestling his first match in a WWE ring in eight years. There are a lot of fans unfamiliar with his work as W. Morrissey and Big Bill, but he is a much better, more polished wrestler than he was nearly a decade ago.

Evans vs. Judgment Day is a logical next step. The question is who will step up and join the babyface against the hated heels.

No. 1 Contender's Match: Penta vs. La Parka

Last Time in Action: Penta defeated Bronco Nima (AAA, August 15); La Parka lost to EK Prosper in a Fatal 4-Way Match (NXT, August 18)

With a date against Rey Fenix in the finals of the No. 1 Contender's Tournament at stake, former Intercontinental Champion Penta battled La Parka in the night's penultimate match-up.

La Parka unloaded his arsenal on Penta, delivering an avalanche Spanish Fly and trying for the Bone Breaker. The latter countered, delivered the Sacrifice, and delivered a springboard Mexican Destroyer to score the win and set up a match with his brother on next week's show.

A fine match that paled in comparison to its predecessor earlier in the show, it was hampered by a lack of drama. Penta has been the obvious tournament winner since the bracket was announced. Losing to La Parka, in the latter's first Monday Night Raw appearance, was never a consideration.

The Lucha Bros explode next week in a match that should be a legitimate contender for WWE TV Match of the Year, if it is given enough time and the siblings are allowed to go all out.

La Parka is such an iconic character that this is one instance where a video package introducing him to the masses would have made for a hotter and more invested crowd.

Last Time in Action: LA Knight, Solo Sikoa, and Royce Keys defeated The Bloodline (SummerSlam, August 1); Jey Uso defeated Sikoa (Raw, August 10)

Royce Keys returned Monday night on Raw and brought OTM's Lucien Price and Bronco Nima with him.

Driven to desperate measures by the attack by The Bloodline that left him bleeding and out of action, Keys led the former NXT tag team in a brutal beatdown of The Usos, LA Knight, and Solo Sikoa, putting an exclamation point on the flagship show.

The shocking return came at the end of a high-profile tag team main event that saw Jimmy and Jey isolate Sikoa before a hot tag to Knight sparked the babyface comeback. Before a winner could be determined, the run-in occurred, resulting in a no contest.

It was a hot close to the show, the crowd in Montreal reacted accordingly, and there is suddenly intrigue at the top of the Raw brand, something there was not an abundance of heading into this week's broadcast.

Suddenly, Keys is a top-tier star, there is an interesting new team around, and The Bloodline's dominance does not look like a given.

Keys showed more personality in this beatdown than he did the entirety of his first few months with the company. That bodes well and shows that there is more to him than being a big, tough heavyweight.

On a night that featured some solid storyline advancement, it was Fenix and Lee's barnburner of a match that stood out and earned the competitors MVP honors.

They took what could have been a forgettable semifinal tournament match and turned it into one of the better TV efforts in a while.

Both are criminally overlooked and underutilized, so hopefully, this is an opportunity to give them something meaningful to do moving forward.

There was a lot to like about this show, with some better-than-expected story stuff, some quality in-ring action, and a big angle at the end of the show to send fans home satisfied.

Not everything hit, but the positive far outweighed the negative, and given the lethargic card for the night, that is a big win in and of itself.

articles.title: Browns Making Another QB Error? 7 Takeaways From Week 2 Of The Preseason
articles.summary: Here's what we learned from this week's preseason games.
articles.body: Two weeks of preseason games are in the books, and we're starting to see the light at the end of the tunnel.  This past week's slate of preseason games, plus joint practices, brought us more glimpses of what we could expect to see in the regular season. But it brought some drama, too. Deshaun Watson was named the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback on Monday after making pointed remarks to the team's fans following his lackluster performance on Saturday. There's also an unusual storyline developing with players who might wind up playing college football in the next couple of weeks.  So, with only one more preseason week to go, here are our takeaways from the latest slate of preseason games.  1. Deshaun Watson Didn’t Deserve The Starting Job In Cleveland. He Got It Anyway. Ralph Vacchiano: Deshaun Watson showed everyone on Saturday why he shouldn’t be the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback, with a terrible on-field performance and an even worse one off the field. Then, Todd Monken gave him the job anyway.  Maybe that’s a sign that the new Browns coach had nothing but bad options in his quarterback competition, but his choice still couldn’t have been any worse. He went with a 30-year-old who’ll surely be an ex-Brown next season over a somewhat promising young quarterback, Shedeur Sanders. And he did it two days after Watson was terrible in a preseason game against the Bills (5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception) and then showed an incredible lack of self-awareness (and an abundance of immaturity) when he whined about being booed. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson said. "It’s a little more personal than that. So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing." OK, that’s a little rich and a lot outrageous, coming from the man who got the biggest fully-guaranteed contract in NFL history from the Browns in 2022 (five years, $230 million) even though he hadn’t played in two years and was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women. He then rewarded that startling generosity by only being healthy enough to play in 19 games over the last four seasons — and not particularly well, either. Even without that bad moment, though, Monken still made the wrong choice. The coach had been leaning this way, multiple team sources told me, in part because the Browns’ early schedule is overloaded with road games (their first two and six of their first nine), and Monken thought Watson’s veteran presence would help his young team. But Watson’s play didn’t warrant that faith. He was just 16 of 27 for 162 yards and an interception in two preseason games. His passer rating of 61.0 was even a notch below Sanders’ 65.2. So while it’s true that there was no good option here, it’s also true that really is no upside to Watson, who is understandably reviled by what seems to be a majority of the Browns’ fan base. Starting Sanders at least would’ve given them hope that he can get better, something to look forward to other than the QB-rich 2027 draft. Instead, Monken latched on to the anchor that has been scraping the Browns along rock bottom for the last five years. Sanders will surely get a shot later this season. But as usual in Cleveland, any hope for the future is delayed. 2. Yes, The Pipeline To The Pros Goes Both Ways Greg Auman: The most backwards trend of the NFL preseason? Marginal players testing the waters of playing in NFL preseason games and  … going back to college. It seems impossible, but these days, if you can get a judge to rule the right way, traditional lines of amateurism and eligibility can disappear. The NCAA’s shift to a five-year eligibility model wasn’t intended to be backdated for athletes who had exhausted their window – and signed a pro contract, gotten paid and even played for NFL teams. But that’s really happening, leaving general managers to wonder if they’ll lose players off their roster to the allure of NIL money from colleges. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright, an undrafted rookie with the Browns, put his name in the transfer portal. Cleveland has since waived him, setting him up to play for LSU this fall. "Man, ain’t this s--- crazy?" Browns coach Todd Monken said. "I mean, I don’t even know what to say … I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know. I didn’t call him back, guess I should have." Speaking of LSU, consider Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted rookie linebacker Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks in Tampa Bay’s preseason opener. He’s also one of the players granted a temporary restraining order that could allow him to return to college football. He played at LSU last year, and that sets up the man-bites-dog possibility of an NFL player leaving early for college. The fall semester at LSU started on Monday, and NFL rosters will be cut from 90 players to 53 by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. It’s unlikely the Bucs will keep Pyburn for their 53, but he has (had?) a good shot at their practice squad. That pays $247,500 for a full season, and Pyburn could make three or four times that much on the Van Wilder go-back-to-college route. Pyburn said after Saturday’s preseason game that his agents had told the Bucs that college was a potential "backup plan," but when pressed as to what he might decide if choosing between an NFL practice squad and going back to college, he was noncommittal. "Ultimately, that’s a decision I’m going to have to make with my family, talk to my agents and see what’s the best business decision and what’s the best option for me and my future career," he said. Yes, it’s NFL "respect my decision" season. Players would have to repay their NFL employers to regain college eligibility. Pyburn got a $15,000 bonus and $100,000 in guaranteed salary, but it’s possible that college NIL payments could also be covered by "offset" language standard in such contracts, normally intended so if NFL Team B pays a player to be on their practice squad, that subtracts from the money NFL Team A was on the hook for by their guarantee. The league will have to sort out the ramifications. Can a player already passed over once in the draft get another shot, like baseball players do? This was already happening with basketball and G League players showing up on college rosters, but for NFL teams, it’s made roster-building even more complicated by the idea that players can make more money playing football at a lower level. 3. Stetson Bennett Commands Offense, Cements Role As Rams' Backup QB Eric D. Williams: With Jimmy Garoppolo no longer on the roster, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s search for someone to fill that void, should reigning MVP Matthew Stafford suffer an injury during the regular season, appears to be over. In the battle between Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett, the Alabama product cracked the door open with a sparkling performance in a Week 1 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs. But Bennett may have closed the door by playing well in a 34-0 victory over the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium. The Georgia product finished with two rushing touchdowns in the first half, leading the Rams to scoring drives on four of his five possessions. Bennett finished 19 of 31 for 181 yards, with no touchdown passes and no interceptions for a 77.5 passer rating.  Ty Simpson also played solidly, finishing 8 of 12 for 73 yards in the second half. Simpson led the offense on one scoring drive. However, Bennett impressed McVay by the way he led the offense, with quarterbacks coach and associated offensive coordinator Dave Ragone calling the plays – although he didn’t like Bennett reaching for the pylon with the ball on his first rushing touchdown. "I loved the fact that he used his legs," McVay said. "We’ll learn from reaching the ball into the end zone, even though I challenged that and we were successful. We don’t want to leave ourselves susceptible to losing the ball out of the end zone where it goes for a touchback. "But he did a great job. I thought he got an opportunity to really showcase a lot of his skills." 4. Daniel Jones Primed To Pick Up From Where He Left Off Last Season Ben Arthur: Watching the Indianapolis Colts quarterback at Wednesday’s joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons, it was impossible for me to tell that he tore his Achilles just eight months ago. Everything you want your passer to do — drop back, scramble, throw on the move, evade pressure — Jones looked normal in doing so. Oh, and he was carving up the Falcons’ secondary as well. With Indianapolis’ rushing attack struggling, Jones was near perfect in the pass game, targeting various receivers.  We still need to see Jones move and perform in games. But all the early signs suggest that he can pick up from last season, when he was playing the best ball of his career before a broken leg slowed him down and the Achilles injury ended his season.  "I think with any major rehab process, you're always kind of progressing and getting back and getting used to doing everything, building up the reps on it, building up just your conditioning level," Jones said Wednesday. "I feel really good and there's nothing I don't feel good doing." The Colts’ pass-catching situation around Jones is a bit shaky at the moment, given star tight end Tyler Warren (groin) and wide receiver Alec Pierce (offseason ankle surgery) are currently sidelined. But when they return, they’ll add to a group that features one of the league’s best slot receivers in Josh Downs and recent signee Keenan Allen, who’s been a dominant force on third down.  That’s a cast of receivers Jones can find success with.  "I think it could be really special, to be honest," Colts coach Shane Steichen said of the pass-catching group. "Alec (Pierce) obviously is a hell of a football player, which you guys know. [Josh] Downs, Tyler [Warren], and then adding Keenan [Allen] to the fold. I think we can do a lot with those guys and move bodies around and find matchups."  5. Let’s Have A Conversation About Chiefs Breakout Rookie WR Cyrus Allen Henry McKenna: If you’ve been following training camp for Kansas City, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re the type who combs X for potential breakout stars in fantasy football, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re obsessed with NFL rookies and the draft, you’ve heard of Allen.  His training camp highlights have been crazy. And Andy Reid didn’t slow the hype’s momentum. "He's done a nice job," Reid said of Allen. "The quarterback trusts him." This was the first week of training camp. Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Louisiana Tech. It felt like a big proclamation, particularly given that Rashee Rice has a history of missing time due to injuries and suspensions and Xavier Worthy has failed to live up to his first-round hype.  Since then, Allen has played well — steadily doing what he could to move up the depth chart. That included scoring touchdowns with the first-team when paired with Patrick Mahomes. That also included beating first-round cornerback Mansoor Delane in 1-on-1s and team drills (7x7 and 11x11), per reporters on the scene. But here’s the truth for anyone expecting the second coming of Tyreek Hill. The folks at Arrowhead Pride broke it down with depth. But it’s likely — perhaps even overly optimistic — to project 60 for Allen. And only six receivers converted 60 targets into 500+ receiving yards in 2025. But before he wows in the box score, he’ll need to land in the WR3 spot. Given that he was playing behind Tyquan Thornton and Jaylen Royals in the second preseason game, Allen appears to be WR5. For what it’s worth, Hill had 83 targets, 61 catches, 593 yards and six touchdowns in his rookie season. That would be a great year for Allen. So keep an eye on him. He’s a real playmaker. But let’s stay reasonable for a rookie in a Chiefs' offense that has a lot of mouths to feed. 6. De’Zhaun Stribling Shows Kyle Shanahan Knows How To Evaluate WRs Williams: NFL draft analysts were up in arms over the San Francisco 49ers taking Ole Miss product De’Zhaun Stribling in the second round, believing the organization had reached for a player that some consensus draft boards had going later in the draft. However, through two weeks of preseason play, Stribling has acquitted himself nicely. Stribling is tied for the league lead with 11 catches for 109 yards, with a long of 32 yards. He finished with four catches for 46 yards in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers this week.  I had a chance to watch Stribling in a joint practice at the Chargers’ facility. At 6-2 and 210 pounds, Stribling is an easy mover with suction-cup hands that can make contested catches in congested areas. Along with that, Stribling has the potential for explosive playmaking ability to do something after the catch, a key attribute in Shanahan’s offense. With Ricky Pearsall out for the year and Brandon Ayiuk no longer on the roster, Stribling should find a significant role in San Francisco’s offense this season. "I love how he handles himself," Shanahan said about Stribling. "He takes coaching well and never seems to take anything personally. He’s been a real fun guy to coach so far." 7. Bills’ Thin WR Corps May Be More Of A Problem Than Ever Vacchiano: One great NFL mystery of this generation will surely be why the Buffalo Bills, with arguably the best quarterback in the league in Josh Allen, keep failing to surround him with top-end receivers. And once again, heading towards a season they hope will end in a Super Bowl, that failure is being exposed. Though they are getting a solid performance this summer from D.J. Moore, the veteran "No. 1" wideout they acquired from the Chicago Bears, the rest of the corps is falling apart. Keon Coleman, their second-best receiver last season (38 receptions for 404 yards and four touchdowns), is nursing a concerning sprained toe. Khalil Shakir, last season’s top wideout (72 receptions for 719 yards and four touchdowns), missed the joint practices and preseason game against the Browns last week with an undisclosed injury. And rookie Skyler Bell, their fourth-round pick, has missed two weeks with a groin injury. That leaves Allen right now with Moore, who cost the Bills a second-round pick in March, Joshua Palmer (22 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns) last season, and … not much else. That, of course, is not how the Bills see it. One team source told me their belief is that Allen can win with almost anyone around him, and that he can take what looks like a below-average group and make them much better. They are also convinced that Moore, at age 29, can reverse his steep, two-year decline simply by playing with an elite quarterback. It’s a gamble, of course, because otherwise all the pieces are in place in Buffalo: A powerful running game led by James Cook, a top offensive line, a top-10 defense that gets a boost from the addition of edge rusher Bradley Chubb. And of course, the brilliance of Allen will always give them a shot. Still, it’s hard not to imagine what this team would look like with just one elite receiver by Allen’s side. It would make their path to Buffalo’s first Super Bowl in 33 years look a lot easier than it currently is.

articles.title: Why 49ers Appear To Be Driving Off The Cliff Entering 2026 Season
articles.summary: During Monday's edition of The Herd, Colin Cowherd evaluated the overall state of the 49ers, questioning whether San Francisco can maintain their position among the elite teams in the NFC.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers enter the upcoming regular season with expectations to remain competitive within arguably the best division in football while battling early injuries, older franchise mainstays returning from surgeries, and, most recently, off-field news involving the team's owner.  That doesn't seem to be a recipe for success, and Colin Cowherd agrees. During Monday's edition of The Herd, Cowherd questioned whether San Francisco can maintain its position among the elite teams in the conference. "I tend to think the Niners are very close to pulling a Thelma and Louise and driving off the cliff here," Cowherd said, comparing the 49ers to the hit '90s movie. On paper, the 49ers have reloaded with talent. They signed star wide receiver Mike Evans to beef up their wide receiver room and brought back Dre Greenlaw to solidify what they have at linebacker.  However, tight end George Kittle continues working back from Achilles surgery with a chance to play in Week 1, and running back Christian McCaffrey remains on a planned load management schedule during practice reps.  With that in mind, Cowherd pointed out that age and recovery timelines across essential positions present distinct hurdles for San Francisco when compared to younger rosters across the league. The roster remains heavily reliant on a core group of established veterans, several of which are returning from surgical procedures. "This is an old, old team, oldest roster in the NFL, and almost all their old guys are coming off serious surgeries," Cowherd said. "They are really dependent on five older players: Trent Williams, left tackle, he's 38. Kittle, going to be a hall of farmer, coming off surgery. Nick Bosa, coming off his second surgery. Christian McCaffrey led the NFL in touches. Mike Evans, who is often banged up, though I love him and Fred Warner off a surgery as well." San Francisco's depth issues have been compounded by injuries to recent high draft selections. "Don't forget their last two first-round picks: Ricky Pearsall, out for the year, injured. … Mykel Williams, who is a great young talent, he's banged up and won't be there for Week 1," Cowherd added. "They are hanging on by peptides and a prayer." Compared to the recent success NFC West rivals the Seahawks and Rams have had in the draft, the Niners will have their work cut out for them. "The Seahawks and the Rams have drafted so brilliantly over the last three years, very few misses. … Those are four games the Niners go in as an underdog," Cowherd said. San Francisco receives early scheduling relief to begin the regular season. Following their trip to Australia, the team returns home for consecutive games against the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals before entering a more challenging stretch that includes matchups against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. Despite the favorable early home slate, Cowherd expressed skepticism regarding San Francisco's postseason prospects over a full 17-game schedule. "I don't think they're a playoff team," Cowherd said. "I love the coach. I love McCaffrey. I love the organization. I think they're heading right for a cliff." articles.title: Blue Demon Jr., luchador: "Por mis lesiones, me metí a estudiar medicina; quiero poner salud en mis compañeros porque sé lo que es estar lastimado"
articles.standfirst: Las desgracias padecidas hicieron más fuerte al 'hijo del demonio azul'
articles.summary: Las desgracias padecidas hicieron más fuerte al 'hijo del demonio azul'
articles.body: La Lucha Libre es un deporte de alta exigencia física y atlética para ejecutar la serie de maniobras, llaves y castigos para llevarse el triunfo sobre los encordados. Sin embargo, cuando se es la víctima ante el rival en turno se expone a una serie de lesiones que lo pueden marginar del ring por un tiempo indefinido sin importar la jerarquía dentro del pancracio. Por ello mismo, el legendario luchador, Blue Demon Jr, tuvo que ponerle pausa a su carrera en diferentes ocasiones debido a las constantes heridas y cirugías a lo largo de su carrera. El 'Hijo del Demonio Azul' prepara su retiro tras más de cuatro décadas en la lucha libre y buscará dedicarse a la medicina regenerativa para ayudar a otros deportistas quienes caigan en las lesiones más comunes de esta actividad. Con alrededor de más de 60 años de edad, el flamante luchador ha impuesto respeto con su fuerza, su carácter y sus movimientos letales. Pero fuera del ring tiene una meta muy noble: sanar al prójimo. Con el pasar de los años, Blue Demon Jr ha buscado tener una preparación académica que la pudiera combinar con su actividad en la Lucha Libre. Tras una infancia de sufrimiento, cumplió su sueño de volar donde a los 18 años de edad se matriculó en el Colegio del Aire y voló una avioneta Cessna y sumó unas dos mil horas de vuelo, el cual le permitía esa libertad que tanto añoró. Una vez en los encordados, también se graduó de sistemas computacionales administrativos. Sin embargo, Blue Demon Jr también superó un cáncer en etapa 4 a los 30 años de edad, donde el doctor que lo atendió le decía que 'avanzara con su papeleo' pues era difícil que lo pudiera superar. Tras vencer esta cruel enfermedad y superar una serie de lesiones, el legendario luchador quiso agradecer a la vida y estudió medicina regenerativa. En unas semanas obtendrá el título y dedicará parte de su tiempo a curar a otros luchadores para que no tiren la toalla y mantengan sus sueños hasta el último segundo posible. El original Blue Demon comenzó un distinguido legado a finales de la década de los 50's e inmortalizado fuera de los encordados con las películas de luchadores a lado del Enmascarado de Plata, el Santo. Al pasar la batuta a su hijo adoptado, la dinastía mantuvo su popularidad hasta transcurrido el siglo XXI donde se ha convertido en un símbolo de su deporte, que en el 2008 ganó el Campeonato Mundial de la NWA (National Wrestling Alliance). Su debut en la lucha libre profesional fue en 1986, después de haber participado con la delegación de México en los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 1984 en la disciplina de Lucha. Con el paso de los años, las lesiones fueron recurrentes. La más grave en estos 40 años fue una fractura en la quinta vértebra lumbar, la cual lo dejó sin movimiento en las piernas durante ocho meses y requirió un proceso de rehabilitación muy difícil en el que incluso tuvo que arrastrarse para moverse. Pasó cerca de seis meses en silla de ruedas debido a este tipo de complicaciones severas. Estas son las lesiones que ha padecido Blue Demon Jr: Entre las victorias más destacadas de Blue Demon Jr fue a los 42 años de edad al derrotar al estadounidense Adam Pierce para convertirse en el campeón mundial de peso completo más longevo de la NWA. En México, sus épicos triunfos contra 'El hijo del Santo', 'Dr Wagner jr' y otros héroes de la lucha libre, serán recordados por siempre y la afición tendrá un años más para disfrutar de Blue Demon Jr antes de colgar la máscara para colocarse la bata de doctor y ayudar a compañeros que hayan caído en las garras del demonio de las lesiones. La gira de Blue Demon Jr. para despedirse comenzará en Irapuato y León, luego se traslada a Monterrey, Ciudad de México, Guadalajara y terminará en Tijuana, ya que fue en esta ciudad fronteriza donde comenzó su carrera profesional. Las carteleras contarán con la participación de Octagón, L.A. Park, Canek Jr, Dr Wagner y Cibernético así como la persona que continuará su legado, su sobrino quien será Blue Demon III.

articles.title: Former Celtics, Jazz Player RJ Luis Jr. Cleared By Judge To Play For LSU
articles.summary: Former St. John's standout RJ Luis Jr. has been cleared by a court to start practicing with LSU and potentially play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body: RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season. Luis, who briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics but never played in an NBA game, hugged LSU coach Will Wade after the ruling by East Baton Rouge Parish District Court judge Ronald R. Johnson. After a five-hour hearing, Johnson granted the player's request for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which had argued Luis was unlikely to win reinstatement after leaving college to turn pro in 2025. "This is precedent. It's monumental," said Baton Rouge-based attorney Tony Clayton, who represented Luis along with Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina. "This allows him to go practice, go play and we'll let the legal process work itself out." The timeline for that process was not immediately clear. "I don't know, but there's a lot of discovery that Elliot and I have to obtain," Clayton said. "We've got a lot of questions." Luis' attorneys noted that the NCAA had granted exceptions allowing numerous players from overseas professional leagues to join college basketball programs, and argued that American players must be afforded the same opportunity. They stressed that Luis not only had never played in an NBA game, but also had not played for the Celtics' G League affiliate because of an injury, and had far less of a professional basketball resume than numerous college players who'd been recruited from abroad. NCAA attorney Taylor Askew argued that Luis' situation was not comparable to those who played for the developmental squads of pro organizations overseas because Luis chose to leave college for the NBA. Askew noted that the only player in a similar situation to Luis was Alabama's Charles Bediako, who won a temporary retraining order allowing him to play five games for Alabama last season before an Alabama judge ultimately sided with NCAA assertions that he was ineligible. "I understand Mr. Luis is disappointed that he was not drafted and did not play in the NBA as much as he would have liked," Askew said. "Actions have consequences. Decisions have outcomes and they're not always the right ones or the ones that you want." As he made his ruling, Johnson said, "In the court's mind, (Luis) did not actually play professional basketball," and that whether Luis was properly advised of his options at the time he left college "lingers heavily before this court." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again. Hankerson signed with the Seahawks last week and rushed for 10 yards on five carries in their 19-16 preseason loss at Tennessee on Sunday night. He also caught two passes for nine yards. He is among 16 players who graduated high school in 2022 and became eligible to play a fifth collegiate season thanks to a Louisiana court order last week. Once he clears waivers, he could enter the transfer portal. Running back T.J. Harden, who played for the Seahawks in their preseason game against Dallas, was also among those granted a temporary restraining order by the Louisiana judge. Harden, who played last year at SMU and went undrafted, was waived by the Seahawks and entered the portal last week. Hankerson was an undrafted rookie out of Oregon State who signed with Miami in April, then was waived earlier this month. He ran for 1,086 yards and nine touchdowns last season, his second in Corvallis. He also had 22 catches for 123 yards. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Angel Reese breaks WNBA record with 26 rebounds in Dream’s win over Sparks
articles.summary: Reese broke Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds and added 11 points for her 27th double-double of the season.
articles.body:
Angel Reese broke the WNBA single-game rebounding record with 26, while also breaking the league’s season record for rebounds, as the Atlanta Dream beat the Los Angeles Sparks.

Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, set on May 23, 2003 for the Washington Mystics, in the Dream’s 78-71 win on Monday .

The Dream star has 458 rebounds this season, seven more than A’ja Wilson’s mark set in 2024.

“Last time I was here, I didn’t miss any shots. Tonight I couldn’t hit (anything), so I knew I was going to be able to get them on the rebounding side,” Reese told the postgame show. “I just want to be there for my team. Offensively, defensively, whatever it takes to win.”

Reese finished with 11 points. She secured her WNBA-leading 27th double-double of the season on a basket with 13.9 seconds left in the game.

“That’s a talent,” Dream guard Allisha Gray said. “I’m just in awe watching her rebound.”

A three-time WNBA All-Star, Reese set a WNBA rookie record with 13.1 rebounds per game and the all-time league record with 15 straight double-doubles with Chicago in 2024. She led the league in rebounding her first two seasons and is leading again this season at 12.0 per game.

The Dream have beaten the Sparks nine straight times.

Gray led Atlanta (25-13) with 20 points. Rhyne Howard added 18 points to eclipse 3,000 for her career. Gray set an Atlanta record for field goals in a season with 247.

Nneka Ogwumike had 27 points and 16 rebounds for Los Angeles (13-25). Dearica Hamby and Cameron Brink each scored 15 points.

articles.title: Fulham vs Chelsea: Alonso starts new era with thrilling 3–2 win
articles.summary: Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer on target as Chelsea open scoring within 31 seconds of the match in London.
articles.body:
Chelsea began life under new coach Xabi Alonso with a breathless 3-2 Premier League victory at West London neighbours Fulham as their exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all found the net.

Chelsea’s first league match of the season got off to a dream start on Monday when Palmer – looking back to his best after struggling with an injury last season – passed to Joao Pedro, and the Brazilian flicked the ball over goalkeeper Bernd Leno 31 seconds into the first half.

It was the quickest goal scored in the opening round of fixtures on Sunday in the Premier League’s 34-year history.

Fulham equalised when Josh King beat goalkeeper Robert Sanchez at his near post in the 24th minute, giving the home fans something to cheer against their fiercest rivals.

But two of Chelsea’s new signings then combined in the 41st as central defender Maxence Lacroix jinked down the right before cutting the ball back to the club’s 117 million pounds ($159.4m) record signing Rogers, who made no mistake.

Four minutes into the second half, Joao Pedro held up the ball in attack and fed Palmer, who angled a shot through Leno’s legs, underlining the midfielder’s return to form after missing out on a place with England at the World Cup.

“It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard,” Palmer told Sky Sports.

“Obviously, with the injuries I’ve had to try and prevent them and work extra hard day in, day out. I know the talent I’ve got, so I can put in performances like that.”

Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia, on his league debut after signing from Real Madrid, gave the hosts some hope by heading in after Sanchez could only parry a Timothy Castagne shot in the 54th.

Fulham then had a great chance to level again through Antonee Robinson in the 78th minute, but his chip over a stranded Sanchez went wide, and Chelsea held out to claim the points.

Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez — a linchpin of World Cup runners-up Argentina , who has been linked with a move to Manchester City — was greeted with loud boos from the home fans when he came on as a substitute midway through the second half.

Alonso’s win in his first competitive match since taking over at Stamford Bridge came at the expense of his former Liverpool and Spain teammate Alvaro Arbeloa — similarly making his Premier League debut as a coach — who also briefly succeeded Alonso as Real Madrid manager last season.

Alonso will hope midfielder Moises Caicedo and new fullback Marco Palestra, who are injured, will provide more solidity, while Sanchez could face an early challenge from Mike Penders, who has returned to Chelsea from sister club Racing Strasbourg.

articles.title: Federer to play tennis at US Open but rules out Williams-like return
articles.summary: The 20-time Grand Slam champion confirmed he’s only going to play in an exhibition match and has no plans to return.
articles.body:
Roger Federer is actually nervous about his tennis.

The man who won five straight US Open championships during the height of his dominance of the sport is set to play again in Arthur Ashe Stadium on Tuesday night for the first time since 2019. And he’s not quite sure how the game that perhaps nobody ever made look more elegant will appear now.

list 3 of 4 Venus Williams hits 13-game tennis losing streak with Cincinnati Open exit
