“I haven’t played a singles set in, I don’t know, [Hubert] Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it’s been five years,” Federer said on Monday, referring to his 2021 quarterfinal loss in his last Grand Slam match.

“I don’t know how it’s going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments.”

It’s only one set of singles in an exhibition against Andy Roddick and one set of doubles with John McEnroe against Roddick and Andre Agassi. The winner of 20 Grand Slam singles titles should be fine for those.

But a return to tennis beyond that, competing in major tennis tournaments in his mid-40s like Venus and Serena Williams?

“No, no, no, no. No, not at all,” Federer said during a news conference.

“Thanks for asking. I wasn’t sure if the question was going to get asked, but I’m happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought.”

At 45, Federer still looks fit, and said he enjoys working out in the gym. But he said he goes through long stretches where he is rarely on the court.

His lengthy absence from the US Open has done little to dampen his popularity, based on the number of people around the grounds who were mentioning his name. The appearance of “Roger Federer” up on the big board for all to see again, before his afternoon practice on Ashe, where Federer collected the trophy every year from 2004-08, was a welcome sight for his fans.

The trip to New York is a stop for Federer on his way to Newport, Rhode Island, where he will be enshrined in the International Tennis Hall of Fame on Saturday.

Federer never really had the chance to say goodbye to New York as a player, because there was no way to know his loss to Grigor Dimitrov in the 2019 quarterfinals would be his last match. He had reached the French Open semifinals and the Wimbledon final earlier that year, falling to Rafael Nadal in Paris and then Novak Djokovic in a fifth-set tiebreaker at the All England Club.

It was easy to imagine him returning to the US Open the next year and making another deep run. But after falling to Djokovic in the semifinals of the Australian Open to begin 2020, he had knee surgery that February, then another procedure in May.

He returned to play in the French Open in 2021 but had to withdraw before his fourth-round match. After the loss to Hurkacz – where he appeared to struggle and lost 6-0 in the third set – Federer had another knee surgery that August and knew there would be no more comebacks.

“The knee can’t do it any more. It’s tired,” he recalled thinking. “The mind can’t be patient even more and wait for another couple years and see what happens.”

Federer knows Tuesday night won’t be real tennis, joking that he and Roddick hopefully would be respectful and not try to drop shot each other. But it will be different from when he did return to Ashe a couple of years back to watch.

“They gave me an ovation because they saw me on the big screen, but I just feel, like, tomorrow and I guess today, as well, and Monday next week, it really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you and goodbye, which I think is important for some,” Federer said.

articles.title: Jai Arrow granted special dispensation to reach South Sydney Rabbitohs century after MND retirement
articles.summary: Jai Arrow, who retired in May following an MND diagnosis, will reach century of appearances for South Sydney Rabbitohs after NRL grant special dispensation for the 31-year-old to feature in Gold Coast Titans and South Sydney games
articles.body:
MND Australia describes it as an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions in which the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and is often called Lou Gehrig's disease.

As part of an agreement with the Rabbitohs, the NRL granted South Sydney special dispensation to include Arrow, 31, as an extra player on Tuesday's official team list and an additional interchange in their rotation for Saturday's game against the Gold Coast Titans.

A similar dispensation will be granted for South Sydney's final regular-season game against the Sydney Roosters.

According to the NRL, Arrow will get dressed in South Sydney playing kit on both matchdays, join the Rabbitohs in the dressing room, lead the team onto the field, become the team's first interchange within seconds of the opening whistle without taking part in any play, and then remain on the interchange bench in his playing kit for the rest of the game.

It will take Arrow's tally to 180 career NRL games and 100 for the Rabbitohs, in addition to his representative appearances for Queensland in the annual State of Origin series.

Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys said it was a chance for the sport to be a "conduit to bring out the best of humanity".

"This thoughtful gesture by the South Sydney Rabbitohs shows the true heart of our game," V'landys said. "Jai has inspired millions of people around the world with the courage and strength he has shown in his fight with MND. He is not only a great player, but an extraordinary person.

"Reaching 100 games for the Rabbitohs is a special achievement, one that Jai, his family and everyone who has supported him should be incredibly proud of. The entire rugby league community stands with Jai and is honoured to celebrate this remarkable milestone with him."

Rugby league star Rob Burrow and Scotland rugby union great Doddie Weir are among the high-profile sportsmen to have died from the illness in recent years.

articles.title: "Julián está atrapado en su propia telaraña"
articles.standfirst: Sólo un perdón público del argentino a la afición del Atlético y que se coma el césped en cada partido podría solucionar su situación
articles.summary: Sólo un perdón público del argentino a la afición del Atlético y que se coma el césped en cada partido podría solucionar su situación
articles.body: El Metropolitano se pronunció y como era de esperar, la hinchada del Atlético de Madrid le mostró el pulgar hacia abajo a Julián Álvarez. La pitada que dedicó al argentino en el partido frente al Villarreal fue como para que 'La Araña' tome ya la decisión que le permitiría escapar de la telaraña en la que él solito se ha enredado. Pero su rictus en el banquillo y su indolencia cuando saltó al terreno de juego en la segunda parte no invitan a pensar que este 'culebrón' vaya a acabar bien. En la última semana de mercado, me da que el 19 del Atleti aún alberga la esperanza de que el club le deje salir porque si no, no se entiende que a esta hora todavía no le haya pedido perdón públicamente a la afición rojiblanca y, aún así, tendría muy difícil lograr el indulto de la parroquia colchonera.  Griezmann se arrepintió del fondo y las formas cuando se marchó precisamente al Barça también y, a base de goles, consiguió cambiar los pitos en aplausos volviéndose a ganar el cariño del Metropolitano. La diferencia es que Antoine ya era un ídolo del Atlético cuando cogió el puente aéreo y su ariete argentino no lo es. De hecho, en su segunda temporada con Simeone ha firmado un curso algo más que discreto. Es más, se tiró casi cuatro meses sin marcar y no recibió ni un reproche de su afición. Esta temporada no va a poder cumplir 'su sueño' de vestir la camiseta azulgrana. Creo que hasta que se resuelva su futuro, no debería jugar más. Está claro que su presencia en el equipo, ahora mismo, resta más que suma. Y después, a apechugar, 'Araña'.

articles.title: Carabao Cup 2026-27: How does prize money work in the competition?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains how prize money works in the EFL Cup
articles.body:
Compared to other cup competitions such as the FA Cup and Champions League, the EFL Cup uses a different payment structure when it comes to prize money for teams.

While most competitions have a structured round-by-round monetary prize, including in its qualifying rounds, the EFL Cup only has specific round prize money from the semi-finals onward.

The EFL Cup winners get Â£100,000 in prize money. For comparison, this season's FA Cup winners will earn just over Â£2.1m in prize money.

Instead of a large prize pot, clubs earn revenue in a number of different ways, with the English Football League seeing those as effectively the competition's prize money.

In the EFL Cup, clubs are offered an equal split of gate receipts regardless of the two teams in the fixture. This can benefit lower league clubs if they are drawn away to a big Premier League side that has a larger stadium than they do.

Should a club sell 40,000 tickets for a match at Â£20 each, it would equate to Â£800,000 in gate receipts.

Clubs can also achieve significant earnings through EFL Cup Facility Fees. This means that clubs can pocket a fee starting from Â£75,000 if their match is shown on Sky Sports' main channel, increasing depending on how far they progress in the competition.

The EFL Cup is worth around Â£110m a season to the EFL, including around Â£70m going to EFL clubs in central payments with additional monies to Premier League and EFL clubs from direct earnings.

articles.title: El Rayo cierra el fichaje de Gnangoro Bouare
articles.standfirst: El club franjirrojo concreta el traspaso del centrocampista del Betis, adelantado por Radio MARCA y MARCA el pasado 12 de agosto, y el jugador firmará por cinco temporadas tras pasar reconocimiento médico
articles.summary: El club franjirrojo concreta el traspaso del centrocampista del Betis, adelantado por Radio MARCA y MARCA el pasado 12 de agosto, y el jugador firmará por cinco temporadas tras pasar reconocimiento médico
articles.body: Lo que MARCA y Radio MARCA adelantó el pasado 12 de agosto ya es una realidad. Gnangoro Bouare va a jugar en el Rayo Vallecano. El centrocampista de Vícar, de 22 años, ya está en Madrid después de que el club franjirrojo haya cerrado este martes su traspaso con el Betis. El jugador pasará reconocimiento médico y firmará un contrato por las próximas cinco temporadas. El movimiento pone punto final a una operación que el Rayo tenía encarrilada desde hace tiempo por una vía muy concreta: la opción preferencial que conservaba sobre el futbolista desde el fichaje de Nobel Mendy. En aquel acuerdo, el club vallecano abonó 500.000 euros para asegurarse una posición de ventaja por Bouare. Ahora, para completar la llegada del centrocampista, ha tenido que pagar alrededor de otros 100.000 euros en concepto de impuestos. La operación también deja al Betis con un porcentaje importante sobre el futuro del jugador. El club verdiblanco se guarda el 50% de los derechos de Bouare y mantiene, además, un derecho de tanteo. Una fórmula que permite al Rayo incorporar a un futbolista que gustaba en Vallecas sin realizar una inversión elevada, mientras el Betis conserva margen de control sobre una posible evolución del centrocampista. Bouare acaba contrato en 2027 y tenía sobre la mesa una oferta del Betis para renovar por tres temporadas más. En Heliópolis habían demostrado que creían en su progresión, pero también eran conscientes del contexto: el jugador tenía mercado, quería definir su futuro deportivo y el Rayo había activado una vía preferencial que terminó siendo decisiva. Gnangoro llegó al Betis en enero de 2025 procedente del Polideportivo El Ejido y fue cedido ese mismo mercado al Atlético Sanluqueño. La temporada 2025-2026 ya la disputó con el filial verdiblanco, con el que jugó 30 partidos antes de dar un paso al frente esta pretemporada aprovechando la salida de Amrabat y ganando presencia en los planes de Manuel Pellegrini. El técnico chileno le dio espacio en una posición de pivote en la que cuenta con Marc Roca y Facundo Bernal, fichado este verano procedente de Fluminense. Bouare respondió con personalidad y se convirtió en una de las apariciones más interesantes del verano bético, hasta el punto de llamar definitivamente la atención del Rayo. El club franjirrojo incorpora a un centrocampista joven, físico y con margen de crecimiento. Un perfil que encaja en la búsqueda de fondo de armario para la medular y que llega a Vallecas después de haber despertado también el interés de clubes de Segunda como Córdoba, Burgos y Cádiz durante este verano. El Rayo, sin embargo, tenía una ventaja heredada del caso Nobel Mendy y la ha terminado aprovechando. Bouare ya está en Madrid, pasará reconocimiento médico y firmará por cinco temporadas. Una operación trabajada desde hace semanas que convierte una opción preferencial en un refuerzo de presente y futuro para Vallecas.

articles.title: El sorprendente favorito para hacerse con la Super Bowl
articles.standfirst: Para Casino Gran Madrid los Rams son el principal candidato
articles.summary: Para Casino Gran Madrid los Rams son el principal candidato
articles.body: La NFL echa a andar su temporada 2026 el próximo 10 de septiembre, apenas siete meses después de que los Seattle Seahawks se proclamaran campeones del Super Bowl LX al imponerse 29-13 a los New England Patriots en el Levi's Stadium, con una exhibición defensiva y una gran noche de Kenneth Walker III, MVP del partido.  Con la pretemporada prácticamente cerrada y los 32 equipos afinando sus plantillas de cara al arranque, las casas de apuestas ya han fijado su jerarquía particular para el Super Bowl LXI, que se disputará el 14 de febrero de 2027 en el SoFi Stadium de Los Ángeles. Casino Gran Madrid ha publicado su lista de favoritos, y hay bastante consenso con lo que ya adelantaban los expertos nada más terminar la pasada final. Y es que, el trono no está garantizado ni para el propio campeón. El gran favorito de la casa de apuestas es Los Angeles Rams, a cuota 6. El equipo de Sean McVay, con Matthew Stafford como MVP de la liga la pasada temporada, llegó hasta la final de conferencia y juega además como local en un Super Bowl que se disputará en su propio estadio, un aliciente extra que el mercado parece haber tenido muy en cuenta a la hora de colocarlo en lo más alto. Le sigue de cerca Buffalo Bills, a cuota 10, con Josh Allen de nuevo como gran estandarte de un proyecto que año tras año se queda a las puertas de la gloria y que vuelve a aparecer entre los máximos aspirantes del mercado. En tercera posición aparecen, empatados a cuota 12, los propios campeones vigentes, Seattle Seahawks, y Baltimore Ravens, el equipo de Lamar Jackson. Que los Seahawks no encabecen el mercado pese a llegar como último campeón no es ninguna sorpresa: la historia reciente de la liga demuestra lo difícil que resulta revalidar el título, con apenas nueve franquicias logrando defenderlo de forma consecutiva, y Seattle afronta además la habitual sangría de bajas en agencia libre que sufren los campeones. Los Ravens, por su parte, siguen siendo un habitual de la parte alta de estos mercados gracias al talento de Jackson, aunque el equipo estrena entrenador esta temporada, una variable que el mercado también pondera. El siguiente escalón lo comparten tres nombres muy reconocibles a cuota 17: Kansas City Chiefs, con Patrick Mahomes buscando demostrar que su ventana de éxito sigue abierta pese a acercarse a los 31 años; Philadelphia Eagles, campeones hace dos temporadas y todavía con plantilla para pelear arriba; y los propios New England Patriots, finalistas la pasada campaña de la mano de un Drake Maye que, pese a la decepción de la final, dejó números de quarterback de época durante la temporada regular. Un peldaño por debajo, a cuota 18, aparecen Los Angeles Chargers y Houston Texans, dos equipos jóvenes con plantillas en plena progresión que el mercado sitúa como aspirantes con opciones reales, aunque todavía a cierta distancia del grupo de cabeza. Cierran la lista de referencia, ya a cuota 20, cinco franquicias con seguimiento habitual en estos mercados: Detroit Lions, Denver Broncos, San Francisco 49ers, Green Bay Packers y Cincinnati Bengals. Ninguno de los cinco parte como favorito claro, pero todos cuentan con plantillas de nivel suficiente como para colarse en la pelea si consiguen mantenerse alejados de la enfermería durante el tramo más exigente del calendario. Con siete meses por delante hasta la cita del SoFi Stadium, el mercado deja claro que, aunque hay un favorito nítido en los Rams, la distancia hasta el resto del pelotón de cabeza sigue siendo relativamente corta.

articles.title: Sir Billy Boston: Trailblazing rugby league player dies aged 92
articles.summary: Trailblazing rugby league player Sir Billy Boston has died at the age of 92; He was the first ever rugby league player to receive a knighthood, ending a 130-year wait for such an honour; He was also the first Black player to represent Great Britain
articles.body:
Back in June 2025, Boston received rugby league's first ever knighthood, ending a 130-year wait for such an honour.

A statement released by Wales Rugby League said: "Today, rugby league has lost one of its greatest-ever players, Wales has lost one of its finest sporting sons, and our sport has lost a truly special gentleman."

The Welsh Rugby Union confirmed his death in a statement, saying: "Sir Billy Boston, one of the best loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport, has passed away peacefully at the age of 92."

Boston blazed a trail for Black sports stars during the 1950s and 1960s, making 488 appearances for Wigan and finishing his career with a British-record 571 tries.

He also became the first non-white player to represent Great Britain on a Lions tour in 1954, scoring 36 tries in 18 appearances in Australia and New Zealand, and featuring in a total of 31 international Test matches.

Boston made a try-scoring debut for Wigan against Barrow in November 1953, and by the time he left the club in 1968, he had played in six Challenge Cup finals at Wembley, featuring on the winning side in 1958, 1959 and 1965.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, an avid follower of the sport, led the tributes to Boston.

Burnham wrote on X : "Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died.

"Billy was one of the greatest rugby league players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet.

"He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan.

"I will miss him greatly and am thinking today of Billy's family, still grieving the recent loss of his beloved wife Joan.

"A giant of a man in every way. Thank you, Billy, and rest in peace."

Wigan have indicated they will pay tribute to Boston prior to their next Super League match against Hull KR on Thursday.

Wigan head coach Matt Peet said: "On behalf of myself, our coaching staff and players, from the first team through to our academy, we send our deepest condolences to Sir Billy's family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

"Billy Boston is woven into the fabric of this club. Every day we walk through the doors, we're reminded that we have a responsibility to represent all those who have gone before us and made Wigan Warriors what it is today. Billy stands at the very top of that history.

"Those fortunate enough to have seen him play tell me he was simply the greatest. His achievements, the man he was and the standards he set will continue to inspire everyone who pulls on this shirt.

"His legacy goes far beyond records and trophies. His impact on Wigan, on rugby league and on the wider sporting world was recognised at the very highest level. We will do everything we can to honour his memory by representing this club with the pride, humility and excellence that he embodied.

"Sir Billy Boston will always be one of Wigan Warriors' greatest sons, and he will never be forgotten."

'One of rugby league's finest' - tributes paid to 'King of Wigan' Boston

"In 1953 he played his first game at Wigan and he became my hero, then my team mate then my friend for 60-odd years.

"I treasure the time I had with Billy - a brilliant player on the field and even better person off the field."

Wigan and Great Britain rugby league legend Shaun Edwards:

"From a working class lad in Cardiff to the King of Wigan - that is Sir Billy Boston."

"When the Wigan representatives stood in the Boston household in Tiger Bay, Cardiff in 1953 and offered Billy a career in rugby league in the North of England it was Billy's mother who told him in no uncertain terms that he would be taking the offer.

"We all have Mrs Boston to thank for giving rugby league one of its finest ever. Billy glowed greatness.

"I have listened to the hardest of rugby league men from Billy's era talk about his presence on the field. The hulking figure they dare not get angry.

"A sensational try scorer who could handle himself if and when the game got physical. Thanks for everything you gave people Billy."

On August 6 1934 in Cardiff, Billy Boston was born to his father John, a seaman from Sierra Leone and his mother Nellie, from the city's Irish community.

Primarily a winger and centre, Boston's rugby career began in the 15-player code in which he represented Wales at youth level.

However, it was not without its struggles. His hometown club Cardiff RFC did not offer him and other Black and mixed-race players a contract.

Such racism also denied him the opportunity to represent Wales and with it, he made the decision to switch codes and join Wigan Warriors.

At 18 years of age in March 1953, Boston signed for Wigan before making his debut eight months later. That would be the first of 488 and crossing the whitewash became customary as he scored 478 tries across that time.

In 1954 more history followed when Boston became the first non-white player to be selected for a Great Britain Rugby League Lions Tour.

Boston became a World Cup winner in 1960, scoring a try in Great Britain's win over Australia and then a second Lions Tour followed in 1962.

His international career saw him score 24 tries across 31 Tests for Great Britain. His other Tour appearances added a remarkable 53 tries in 27 games.

After 16 years with Wigan, Boston joined Blackpool Borough and made 11 appearances and scored five tries, ending his domestic career with 499 appearances.

Boston's career ended at 36 years of age and the statistics are staggering. He scored 571 tries, the second most in rugby league history.

A rugby league immortal, he has three statues - situated in Wales, Wigan, and at Wembley Stadium.

articles.title: 20 Athletes Whose Career Earnings Would Shock You
articles.summary: NBA veteran James Harden recently made headlines when a new three-year, $97 million deal with the Cavaliers put him on track to break the $500 million mark for career earnings.
articles.body:
NBA veteran James Harden recently made headlines when a new three-year, $97 million deal with the Cavaliers put him on track to break the $500 million mark for career earnings.

That raised an immediate question: Which other athletes have career earnings that would shock the average fan? Off we went to scour the all-time leaderboards at Spotrac to find the answer.

This is a subjective exercise, but if a name immediately comes to mind as handsomely paid relative to his body of work, there's a good chance he isn't featured here since the focus was shock value.

For example, Tobias Harris (NBA), Kirk Cousins (NFL) and Stephen Strasburg (MLB) are prime examples of players whom general sports fans would be quick to associate with massive paydays.

However, the following 20 players should be a genuine shock, including four legendary retired athletes whose surprisingly low figures provide a counterpoint to their highly paid counterparts.

Note: All salary figures reflect all money on the books, including future earnings.

With a new three-year, $97 million contract on the books to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, James Harden is officially on track to join a short list of NBA players who have earned $500 million by the time the 2028-29 season arrives.

Harden split his age-36 season between the Los Angeles Clippers and Cavaliers last year. He continues to contribute at a high level after averaging 23.6 points and 8.0 assists while knocking down 37.5 percent of his attempts from distance.

He enters the 2026-27 campaign ranked 11th on the NBA's all-time scoring list with 29,339 points in 17 seasons.

The massive five-year, $251 million extension that Bradley Beal signed prior to the 2022-23 season helps prop up his massive career earnings total, but it's still shocking to see that number north of $400 million.

The three-time All-Star peaked at 31.3 points per game during the 2020-21 season, when he also earned his only All-NBA selection as a third-team choice. However, he has never advanced beyond the conference semifinals.

The 33-year-old signed a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the Clippers in mid-August, although he's also receiving $19.4 million annually from the Phoenix Suns through 2029-30 after they waived and stretched him in 2025. He played just six games last year before undergoing season-ending surgery to repair a fractured hip.

Danilo Gallinari is perhaps best remembered as the centerpiece whom the New York Knicks sent to the Denver Nuggets in their trade for Carmelo Anthony during the 2010-11 season.

At the time, Gallinari was a 22-year-old in his third NBA season who was averaging 15.9 points per game. By the time the 2015-16 season rolled around, he was the leading scorer (19.5 PPG) for a Nuggets team that finished 33-49.

A three-year, $64.8 million sign-and-trade deal that sent him from the Nuggets to the Los Angeles Clippers in 2017 was the largest individual contract that Gallinari ever signed, but he still managed to eclipse the $200 million mark over his 14-year career.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

After Jakob Poeltl served as a valuable bench piece for the Toronto Raptors during the 2017-18 season (his second year in the NBA), the Raptors traded him to the San Antonio Spurs along with DeMar DeRozan in their blockbuster deal to acquire Kawhi Leonard the following summer.

He spent five seasons with the Spurs before ultimately finding his way back to Toronto in 2023. That summer, he inked a four-year, $78 million deal with the Raptors, and he signed a three-year, $84 million extension two years later.

The 7-footer has been a solid role player, but with career averages of 9.1 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocks, it is surprising to see he has racked up over $200 million in career earnings.

An NBA champion with both the Los Angeles Lakers (2019-20) and Denver Nuggets (2022-23), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has carved out a rock-solid career as a three-and-D wing, even with some inconsistency in his shooting.

After spending four seasons each with the Detroit Pistons and Lakers to begin his career, he is set to suit up for his fifth team in the last six years after inking a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers during the offseason.

A three-year, $66 million contract from the Orlando Magic stands as KCP's largest single payday, but his staggering career earnings have been more about steady production over his 13-year run in the NBA.

The Thunder signed Isaiah Hartenstein to a three-year, $87 million deal prior to the 2024-25 season despite his modest career averages of 6.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 18.0 minutes per game.

He immediately thrived in an expanded role, averaging 11.2 points, 10.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks for a Thunder squad that finished 68-14 and won the NBA championship.

Productive bigs don't grow on trees, but a player who has averaged double-digit points only once in his career banking more than $150 million stands out as shocking nevertheless.

Michael Jordan signed an eight-year, $25.7 million deal prior to the 1988-89 season. He made only slightly more than teammates Toni Kukoč ($3.56M), Ron Harper ($3.12M), Scottie Pippen ($2.925M) and Dennis Rodman ($2.5M) with a $3.85 million salary in the final year of that contract in 1995-96.

His Airness re-upped with the Bulls on a one-year, $30.14 million contract the following year, which made him the highest-paid athlete in American sports history at the time. But spending the bulk of his career playing on that modest eight-year deal left Jordan's career earnings below $100 million.

Don't shed too many tears for MJ, though. His net worth stands at an estimated $4.3 billion thanks in large part to his Nike, Hanes and Gatorade deals, along with selling his majority stake in the Charlotte Hornets.

With a 3.93 ERA and 108 ERA+ over 1,852.2 career innings, Aaron Nola has been a staple in the Philadelphia Phillies' rotation for more than a decade after the club took him No. 7 overall in the 2014 draft.

However, Nola has made just one All-Star team during that time while receiving Cy Young votes on four occasions. He peaked at third in the balloting during the 2018 season, when he had a 2.37 ERA and 224 strikeouts in 212.1 innings.

The seven-year, $172 million deal to re-sign him shortly after he hit the open market following the 2023 season accounts for a significant chunk of Nola's career earnings, but that's still a shocking figure for a pitcher who's rarely mentioned among the game's elite.

Thanks to a standout glove and some solid pop for a middle infielder, Marcus Semien has racked up 49.7 WAR over 14 seasons in the majors.

That included a five-year stretch from 2019-23 where his 29.3 WAR trailed only Mookie Betts (30.3) among all players, though he has rarely been considered a bona fide superstar at any point in his career.

Now in the fifth season of a seven-year, $175 million deal, Semien has struggled through the worst season of his career after being traded to the New York Mets last offseason. He is still owed $46 million over the final two seasons of his contract.

A five-year, $86 million deal that was the richest ever for a reliever at the time and the longevity to still be one of the best relievers in baseball at the age of 38 have helped Aroldis Chapman put up the highest career earnings of any relief pitcher.

He has been an All-Star each of the past two seasons since joining the Red Sox, posting a 1.46 ERA with 61 saves in 112 appearances. That puts him in a strong position to surpass the $200 million mark before he calls it a career.

What sort of deal will Mason Miller command once he reaches free agency if he continues to pitch at the elite level he has shown for the San Diego Padres?

As a two-time All-Star who has received Cy Young votes just once in his 15-year career, Nathan Eovaldi is an unlikely inclusion on a list of the highest-paid pitchers in MLB history.

With a 3.91 ERA and 105 ERA+ across 1,835 innings, he has put together a solid big league career. A postseason resume that includes a 9-3 record with a 3.05 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 82 strikeouts in 79.2 innings does help elevate his profile.

Still, his $185.8 million career earnings will slot in ahead of Randy Johnson ($177.0M) on MLB's all-time leaderboard once his current three-year, $75 million deal is fully paid out.

Cal Ripken Jr. was baseball's "Iron Man" with 2,632 consecutive games played. He was far more than just durable with 3,184 hits, 431 home runs, 1,695 RBI and 95.9 WAR en route to Cooperstown.

Despite a career that stretched from 1981 through 2001, the five-year, $32.5 million extension he signed during the 1992 season was the largest deal he inked during his storied career.

His career earnings put Kyle Tucker's $60 million AAV with the Los Angeles Dodgers into perspective, even if we are comparing players across different eras.

Anže Kopitar spent his entire 20-year career with the Los Angeles Kings before retiring after the 2025-26 season. The two-time Stanley Cup winner will go down as one of the best two-way forwards of his era.

However, it's still surprising to see that he currently stands as the fourth-highest-paid player in NHL history , behind only Alex Ovechkin ($170.7M), Sidney Crosby ($165.7M) and Evgeni Malkin ($151.7M).

Granted, Kopitar is projected to fall to No. 10 on that list by the time the 2030-31 season rolls around and some of the game's current stars continue to climb the career-earnings leaderboard.

A huge 13-year, $98 million deal with the Minnesota Wild serves as the backbone of Ryan Suter's impressive career earnings. A 20-year career helped push that total above the nine-figure mark.

His resume is built more on longevity and durability than top-tier accolades. He played in 1,526 games, but he never won a Stanley Cup and never took home any individual hardware.

He has not formally retired, though he didn't play during the 2025-26 season after his contract was bought out by the Dallas Stars.

When Wayne Gretzky signed his three-year, $25.5 million deal with the Los Angeles Kings, his $8.5 million AAV more than doubled the NHL's previous top earner. However, that still wasn't enough to push his career earnings over $50 million.

He also signed an absurd 21-year personal services contract with the Edmonton Oilers early in his career that was ultimately reworked, but his earnings stretched beyond what he made for his time on the ice.

With an estimated net worth of $250 million , he maximized his earning potential with endorsements from brands like Coca-Cola, Nike and McDonald's.

Between a four-year, $160 million deal from the New York Giants that ultimately ended in his release and a two-year, $88 million contract from the Indianapolis Colts, Daniel Jones has quietly put together a staggering career earnings total.

The No. 6 overall pick in the 2019 draft looked like a star in the making when he threw for 3,027 yards and 24 touchdowns as a rookie, but that ended up being his peak in a Giants uniform.

The Colts plucked him from the scrapheap after he was released by the Giants with a one-year, $14 million deal, and he earned his second major payday thanks to a 3,101-yard, 19-touchdown performance over 13 games before he suffered a right Achilles tear.

The son of Hall of Fame lineman Bruce Matthews and part of a Matthews family tree loaded with football talent, left tackle Jake Matthews went No. 6 overall in the 2014 draft and immediately slotted in as Matt Ryan's blindside protector.

Matthews has started 196 consecutive games over 12 seasons in the NFL, which stands as the longest active streak in the NFL. However, he has made just one Pro Bowl and zero All-Pro teams along the way.

With four Super Bowl rings and legendary status, Joe Montana is generally mentioned among the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history.

The four-year, $13 million extension he signed prior to the 1990 season made him the highest-paid player in football at the time, which is a perfect snapshot of just how much quarterback salaries have skyrocketed in the last 35 years.

There were 18 quarterbacks during the 2025 season who earned more than Montana did over the course of his entire 17-year career.

articles.title: WWE Raw Just Got Exciting Again After Shock Debut and More Fallout Including a Booking Fail
articles.summary: As WWE ramps up for a journey to Mexico City next month, the August 24 edition of Raw on Netflix delivered spectacle from the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
articles.body:
As WWE ramps up for a journey to Mexico City next month, the August 24 edition of Raw on Netflix delivered spectacle from the Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa.

LA Knight and Solo Sikoa challenged The Usos only to be attacked by the returning Royce Keys and his new allies from NXT, OTM.

Penta and Rey Fénix advanced to the finals of the luchador No. 1 contender tournament in great matches with La Parka and Dragon Lee, respectively.

This and more highlighted an exciting show for Raw that might have set the red brand back on track.

Massive Shocker Changes Everything on Raw

While it looked like the battle lines in WWE were set as Solo Sikoa and LA Knight collided with The Bloodline, a new group has arrived to shake things up.

Despite previously working with Sikoa and Knight, Royce Keys led an attack alongside Bronco Nima and Lucien Price from NXT against the popular babyfaces.

This sets the stage for three conflicting sides to battle on Raw, elevating multiple underused names on Raw who could soon be seen as top stars.

In particular, this heel turn makes Keys feel like a real threat for the first time since his WWE arrival, and he is backed by two talented, hungry newcomers in OTM.

With the consistently growing popularity of Knight and Sikoa, any heels who contest them will get heat.

This also gives the conflict with The Bloodline, which was already running out of steam, new life as fresh faces are caught in the mix.

Suddenly, anything can happen, and all WWE needs to do is stay unpredictable. That has been difficult for the company previously, though.

Stephanie Vaquer Shows Exactly Why WWE Needs Her

Stephanie Vaquer is back in the action, and she looked great against Roxanne Perez, clearly working at her physical peak again in the ring.

These are the kind of matches that keep fans invested in the Raw women's division, highlighting the talent that can perform at the highest level.

La Primera can deliver this performance against anyone on Raw, and WWE should let her do so.

Do not simply keep her in a backstage segment after a likely loss to Liv Morgan. She should be wrestling.

WWE should find ways from singles to tag to six-man action to keep stars like Vaquer, Perez, Iyo Sky, Sol Ruca and more wrestling at least every other week.

While the women's division on Raw still feels understaffed with numerous absences, the teased arrival of Lola Vice soon should help.

The former NXT women's champion will be a quick hit on the main roster due to her hard-hitting in-ring style and flashy presentation.

Vice is a star both in style and talent that can instantly elevate the midcard women's division while she establishes her name.

In particular, pitting her against Women's intercontinental champion Raquel Rodriguez gives an important fresh challenger to that title scene.

She and Sol Ruca can serve as the primary babyfaces to capture the gold while Lyra Valkyria and Roxanne Perez are the main heel threats.

This is a strong foundation built off recent years of NXT and suddenly makes this division look relevant.

If WWE really wants to make Vice shine off the bat, it would make sense for her to even take the gold from Rodriguez, even just in a short reign like Ruca's.

With the championship switching hands, it will be clear that anyone on this roster is a threat to capture the gold at any time.

He has beat up and slowed the momentum of Je'Von Evans, who was already the slowest riser of the fresh NXT call-ups.

At most, his threat also extends to luchadors like Penta, Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio, but the big man beating up the smaller competitors is not compelling storytelling on its own.

Cass has more charisma than he has showcased so far, even if the plan is not for Enzo Amore to join him on Raw.

He could at least talk as much as Baron Corbin has on SmackDown, who is awkwardly looking like the better fit in the same role as Cass.

If WWE does not find a way to showcase Cass' personality soon, he is going to become a lost cause, falling back into the pack like Rusev and Ethan Page before him.

If WWE needs fresh names on Raw who can instantly work crowd-pleasing matches, there is no better place to look than AAA.

La Parka, El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr., Psycho Clown, Laredo Kid and El Fiscal all delivered in their spots for the No. 1 contender tournament.

The only shame was that WWE had not highlighted them all more before this to sell them as real threats to win over the luchadors working Raw and SmackDown.

Raw could use a good 20-minute block weekly for AAA luchadores to showcase their talent against established Raw stars.

Add in El Hijo del Vikingo and Octagón Jr. when they are healthy alongside more opportunities for Mr. Iguana, and the rotation of luchadores could become the spectacle match Raw needs.

This is not even mentioning the possibility of Flammer, Lady Shani, La Catalina and Faby Apache adding fresh names to the women's division rotation.

AAA is a company owned and run by WWE. Why not try to elevate the talent in AAA while making Raw better weekly?

articles.title: Ex-Wimbledon champion Vondrousova appeals to CAS over four-year doping ban
articles.summary: The Czech was issued a suspension in June after she did not submit her sample when notified by a doping control officer.
articles.body:
Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against her four-year ban for missing a doping test last year, the sport’s highest judicial body said.

CAS on Tuesday confirmed the receipt of the appeal and said a hearing had not yet been scheduled. Vondrousova’s ban ends on June 21, 2030, when she will be 30.

Vondrousova was issued the suspension in June after the International Tennis Integrity Agency said the Czech did not submit her sample when notified by a doping control officer in an out-of-competition test attempt at her home in December.

The 27-year-old said in April she had “reached a breaking point after months of physical and mental stress” and added that an officer arriving at 8:15pm demanding an immediate test felt like a serious intrusion into her privacy.

Vondrousova has said she never doped , and a test taken three days after the December 3 incident came back negative.

The former world number six has not played since skipping the Adelaide International in January due to a shoulder injury and has dropped to world number 153.

She won the 2023 Wimbledon title, having previously made the French Open final in 2019 and bagged a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Luke Littler and Michael van Gerwen to headline £450k event as full 32-player field confirmed
articles.summary: A top prize of £100,000 will be up for grabs at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals, with Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price set to headline blockbuster 32-player field, with tournament set to commence on September 17
articles.body:
The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.

Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.

Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.

He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final .

World Matchplay champion Littler enters the tournament as the third seed, while Price, who was beaten by the 19-year-old in the final at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool , is the second seed.

Luke Humphries also joins the 32-player field as the fourth seed, after he claimed victory at the US Darts masters in June, while New Zealand Darts Masters winner Jonny Clayton and Australian Darts Masters champion James Wade are seeded sixth and seventh, respectively.

Gian van Veen and Stephen Bunting, seeded fifth and eighth, make up the final seeded players on the list.

Those inside the top 24 of the final World Series rankings will gain a berth to play in Amsterdam.

Australian Brody Klinge, who was beaten by Wade in the final of the Australian Darts Masters, will make his debut at the World Series of Darts Finals .

Nathan Aspinall, Josh Rock and Danny Noppert will also join the field, while Ross Smith, who won the Players Championship 20 in June after picking up his maiden European Tour title earlier in the year is also in the field.

Ryan Searle, Wessel Nijman, Chris Dobey and Jermaine Wattimena have also gained tickets to Amsterdam as the four top non-qualified players from the PDC World Rankings as of August 23.

The field was confirmed following Monday night's Tour Card Holder Qualifier in which Rob Cross was among four names to book their place at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Cross bested Dirk van Duijvenbode in Leicester to book his place in Amsterdam, and was joined by Kevin Doets, as well as Karel Sedlacek and Callan Rydz, who will both make their debuts at September's event.

The first round of the tournament will commence over two sessions on Thursday 17 and Friday 18 September, before round two begins on Saturday, September 19.

The finals will then begin on Sunday, September 20, with the quarter-finals set to get under way in the afternoon, before the semi-finals and final later in the evening.

articles.title: Sir Billy Boston: 'A world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told'
articles.summary: Rugby league commentator Matt Newsum says Sir Billy Boston was a "world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told".
articles.body:
When Sir Billy Boston was knighted in 2025, it was a unique moment for rugby league.

For the first time, this rebel sport from the north of England had been recognised in such a manner; one of its heroes had been acknowledged for their contribution to history through the game.

Sir Billy was a fitting recipient of the honour and a world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told.

You can tell the importance of someone by how many statues have been erected in tribute, and Sir Billy Boston wasn't lacking.

His name was chosen as one of just five to grace Wembley's monument to rugby league's Challenge Cup, while years after his departure north, his home city of Cardiff also ensured his legacy remained cast-iron strong as he formed part of a three-man tribute along with Clive Sullivan and Gus Risman.

Unsurprisingly, Boston is also captured in bronze in his adopted home of Wigan; the place where his legend really came to life.

Born and brought up in Cardiff's ethnically-eclectic Tiger Bay district, he learned his rugby skills on the streets and with the talent factory-esque Cardiff International Athletic Club.

Like all Welsh lads he harboured dreams of playing for his local club Cardiff RFC and hopefully the national team.

Like others before and after for a time, Boston found those routes blocked, having to travel to Neath and Pontypridd to trial before his military service took him north.

It was here where the league scouts came calling, and Wigan persuaded Boston to turn professional in 1953, forever ending his union dreams in the time of 'sine die' penalties for liaising with league personnel.

Â£3,000 could easily buy a house at that stage, while it proved money well spent as he took to the new code like a duck to water, scoring with his first touch in a Wigan A team game.

This prime specimen of Welsh breezeblock had everything; he was quick, he could step and as former player and BBC commentator Ray French put it - his fend was like "being hit in the face with shovel".

The sepia footage and slow shutter speeds of the cameras that captured his magic during his playing days simply cannot dull his brilliance.

Whether it was bustling over for another try in cherry and white hoops at Wembley or crushing the Aussies at Sydney Cricket Ground, Boston was a blur of speed, footwork and power.

Having swiftly progressed to the first team at Central Park, he would go on to score 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, and tales of his feats would be passed down through generations. There are very few down at the Brick Community Stadium these days who don't know of Sir Billy, young or old, his name carried a cache right until his last.

Great Britain gave him the international recognition denied to him by Wales, and he rewarded the selectors by racking up the tries, particularly against the Australians who would bear the brunt of his scoring ability.

He scored 36 tries alone on his maiden Great Britain tour, dazzling both Australia and New Zealand in 1954 under captain and fellow Welshman Dickie Williams.

Boston was a phenomenal rugby league player, but there is also a powerful message in how in post-war Britain a black athlete could become a hugely popular figure by communities adjusting to a new, more diverse world.

Others like Roy Francis beforehand, Johnny Freeman, and Colin Dixon, also became established names, but never quite sprinkled the same stardust as Sir Billy.

It paved the way for players such as Ellery Hanley and Martin Offiah to charm the public with their talents, while modern day talent such as Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul continues to stand out in a sport which has broken down barriers for years.

Sir Billy had a unique unifying effect on a normally partisan and tribal rugby league community.

He was revered naturally in Wigan, his adopted home, but you won't hear a boo or jeer at mention of Boston anywhere - not even at sworn rivals St Helens where they appreciate a good footballer when they see one.

Still a regular visitor to Wigan games right up to his passing, it was always a beautiful moment when the cameras found him, the crowd spotting him on the screen bursting into cheer, and the realisation creeping over his face in the shape of a smile.

There was a photo of him and his wife Lady Joan, who had died just a few weeks previously, on her seat with flowers at Wigan's game with Wakefield last week. There is a poignancy that Sir Billy departed soon after her.

His seat will always be reserved at Wigan, and he will be dearly missed but certainly not forgotten.

articles.title: How did Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin reportedly collect 33 traffic fines in Russia
articles.summary: NHL News: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin reportedly collected 33 traffic fines in Russia during his offseason, totaling around 82,000 rubles. The fines were for various offenses and have sparked interest due to Ovechkin's celebrity status.
articles.body: Alex Ovechkin reportedly had an unusually high number of traffic violations in his native Russia during a portion of his NHL offseason. According to reports from Russian outlet Mash Sport, the Washington Capitals captain has been fined 33 times over the course of roughly four months. The total reported was 82,000 rubles, or about $1,000 at current media conversions.The alleged violations occurred during Ovechkin's absence from the NHL over the summer. They allegedly included speeding, toll-road violations, unpaid parking fines and stopping or parking in restricted areas. The attention around the story hasnât been on the financial value of the penalties, but rather on the sheer quantity of citations.Why did Alex Ovechkin reportedly receive traffic fines in Russia?During the NHL offseason, Alex Ovechkin was reportedly fined for multiple traffic violations in Russia. The 33 citations were connected to his Aurus Arsenal, a luxury Russian minivan tied to the Washington Capitals star, reports said.The citations reported were for multiple offences, not one repeated offence. One of the infractions was speeding, while other reports also mentioned toll road fines, parking tickets and stopping or parking in restricted areas. All in all, it came to 82 thousand rubles.That means the headline figure of 33 fines does not necessarily equate to 33 separate police stops. Available reports indicate the infractions were traffic-related citations tied to Ovechkinâs vehicle while in Russia for an extended period.Why did Alex Ovechkin reportedly receive traffic fines in Russia?According to reports, Ovechkin has already paid most of the reported fines. One citation was still reported outstanding, worth 4,500 rubles.The number of violations makes the incident unusual, though itâs a relatively small financial penalty in relation to the scale of Ovechkinâs NHL earnings. The 40-year-old forward is still one of the NHLâs most recognisable players, so an off-season stat that included 33 traffic tickets was bound to get some attention.Traffic reports donât mention an NHL suspension, hockey-related discipline, injury or roster issue with the Washington Capitals. Instead, the incident happened away from NHL competition during Ovechkinâs off-season in Russia.Ovechkin will return to Washington for his 22nd NHL season after signing a new one-year contract with the Capitals. He comes into the campaign after scoring 32 goals and 32 assists in 82 games in 2025-26.The timing is odd because Ovechkin has otherwise been spending his offseason preparing for another NHL season. When the new season begins, he will again be a center of attention for the Washington Capitals, who made him the NHLâs all-time regular-season goals leader.For now, the 33 traffic tickets reported are an unusual offseason footnote for a player whose career stats usually center on goals, records and championships.The reports also make it clear that this is about traffic violations, not a legal issue related to his NHL career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tottenham sign Brazilian winger Savinho from Manchester City
articles.summary: Savinho’s arrival, which comes in a busy transfer window for Spurs, takes their spending past $400m.
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur have signed Brazil winger Savinho from Manchester City in a deal that takes their close-season spending above 300 million pounds ($409m) under manager Roberto De Zerbi, having just escaped relegation last term.

Both clubs confirmed the transfer on Monday, but the financial details and length of contract were not disclosed. British media last week reported that the deal was worth 75 million pounds ($102.2m) and included a further 10 million pounds ($13.63m) in add-ons.

list 2 of 4 Arsenal face Man City in Community Shield before EPL return – all to know

list 3 of 4 Marmoush brace helps Man City defeat Atletico Madrid in South Korea

list 4 of 4 Man City beat Palace to close gap with Arsenal to 2, with two games to play

“[Savinho] is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity,” De Zerbi said in a statement.

“We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.”

Savinho started at Atletico Mineiro and joined Troyes in 2022, but his breakout season came on loan at Girona, where he scored 11 goals in 41 appearances as they finished a club-high third in La Liga in 2024 and qualified for the Champions League.

He moved to City in the close season that year and has since made 84 appearances in all competitions, scoring seven goals. The 22-year-old has also played 13 times for Brazil.

Savinho is the latest arrival at Spurs in a busy transfer window that has included the signings of midfielders Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, plus defenders Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Savinho’s transfer takes the North London club’s outlay up to 322 million pounds ($438.9m), if the add-ons in the deal are included, as they revamp the squad after finishing a lowly 17th last season.

According to British media, Spurs are also in talks over a move for City’s Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush.

Tottenham began the Premier League campaign with a 3-0 loss at Brentford on Saturday. They next host Championship (second-tier) Charlton Athletic in the League Cup second round on Wednesday before hosting Newcastle United on Saturday.

articles.title: Al volante del Audi más bestia de la historia: 1.001 CV y más rápido que un Lamborghini
articles.standfirst: Hemos conducido el Nuvolari, el Audi de calle más extremo de la historia: 1.001 CV, 351 km/h, DRS y una producción limitada a 499 unidades.
articles.summary: Hemos conducido el Nuvolari, el Audi de calle más extremo de la historia: 1.001 CV, 351 km/h, DRS y una producción limitada a 499 unidades.
articles.body: Para desarrollar desde cero el superdeportivo más potente de su historia, Audi utilizó sus recursos internos para tenerlo listo en tan solo 405 días (poco más de un año), contando desde la primera reunión en la que se aprobó el proyecto. Más concretamente, recurrió a Lamborghini y tomó prestados el chasis y el motor del reciente superhíbrido enchufable Temerario. Para bautizarlo, recurrió al nombre de Tazio Nuvolari, un piloto italiano de enorme talento de las décadas de 1930 y 1940, ganador de carreras de motociclismo, Le Mans, la Mille Miglia y Grandes Premios. En este último caso, a finales de la década de 1930, A finales de la década de 1930, pilotaba monoplazas de Auto Union (la marca que más tarde estaría en el origen de Audi). Su nombre ya se había utilizado en el prototipo que fue precursor de un Audi de producción en 2003, y ahora revive en el que es el coche de producción más potente de la historia de Audi, limitado a 499 unidades. Y con un precio superior a 600.000 euros por unidad. Tecnológicamente, no deja de ser un concepto cercano al de los monoplazas de Fórmula 1 y los prototipos de resistencia actuales, que combina una enorme potencia de propulsión de combustión con la ayuda de la energía eléctrica para mejorar el rendimiento y la tracción, además de incorporar elementos de aerodinámica activa. Y, en este contexto, se posiciona para cumplir el viejo lema del automovilismo de "ganar el domingo para vender el lunes". El Nuvolari es el primer vehículo de producción que adopta la nueva filosofía de diseño de Audi (que, cronológicamente, debutó en el Concept C), y destaca por sus superficies tensas y la configuración de motor central/trasero que define sus proporciones y su volumen monolítico. La carrocería impacta igualmente con el nuevo color exclusivo de Audi, Titanio, utilizado también en el Audi Concept C y en el monoplaza de Fórmula 1. Detrás de esta filosofía de diseño más minimalista (denominada "Radical next") se encuentra Massimo Frascella, el italiano que comenzó su carrera en Bertone, pasó por el Grupo Ford, lideró el diseño de Jaguar/Land Rover y fue contratado a principios del verano de 2024 para definir las líneas de los futuros Audi. “Cada elemento externo cumple una función aerodinámica bien definida, desde el alerón delantero hasta el difusor trasero. Y todo es tal como se ve, ya sea fibra de carbono o aluminio, tanto en el exterior como en el interior”, explica Gael Buzyn, director del centro de diseño avanzado de Audi en Malibú, EE. UU., con quien compartí esta primera experiencia dinámica con el Nuvolari. También llama la atención que la carrocería esté prácticamente desprovista de aristas afiladas, pero eso no significa que su excepcional rendimiento no quede anticipado por sus formas monolíticas y limpias, a diferencia de lo que vemos en un Lamborghini. “La colaboración entre diseñadores e ingenieros fue fundamental, asegurando que cada elemento de la carrocería tuviera una razón de ser funcional”, añade el diseñador francés, quien lleva 20 años afincado en Estados Unidos. En este sentido, "la colaboración de los pilotos del equipo de Fórmula 1, Nico Hülkenberg y Gabriel Bortoleto, fue fundamental durante la fase de desarrollo de este proyecto", como destacó Viktor Underberg, director de Rendimiento de Coches Deportivos de Audi, quien fue mi copiloto durante los aproximadamente 10 kilómetros de esta experiencia exclusiva al volante del Nuvolari. Bortoleto, por ejemplo, mencionó durante el desarrollo dinámico que lo que inmediatamente le llamó la atención en las pruebas de Nardò fue la precisión y previsibilidad del coche en las curvas: "Básicamente, no hay subviraje, lo que es impresionante dado el nivel de rendimiento. El equilibrio se mantiene muy neutro y preciso, lo que proporciona la confianza necesaria para mantener la velocidad en las curvas. Se puede sentir claramente cómo los diferentes sistemas, especialmente la aerodinámica y la distribución del par, trabajan en conjunto", explicó el brasileño.  Underberg (quien había trabajado previamente en Audi antes de su paso por Lamborghini en los últimos años) destaca que "se prestó una enorme atención al equilibrio entre la carga aerodinámica y la resistencia para maximizar la estabilidad y, por consiguiente, permitir un control preciso del Nuvolari". El chasis, la suspensión y la distancia entre ejes son los mismos que los del Temerario, con un ligero aumento del ancho de vía de 1 cm delante y 2 cm detrás. El S-Duct delantero (que entra por el parachoques y sale por el capó) proporciona carga aerodinámica adicional, reduciendo la sustentación a altas velocidades y mejorando la refrigeración del motor. Pero el elemento central del sistema de aerodinámica activa es el ala trasera adaptativa retráctil, que controla la fuerza descendente y la resistencia aerodinámica en tres configuraciones: cerrada, carga baja (low downforce) y carga alta (high downforce). En la posición Cerrada, el ala trasera se retrae para minimizar la resistencia aerodinámica y mejorar la eficiencia. En las configuraciones de alta y baja carga se generan diferentes niveles de carga aerodinámica según la dinámica de conducción y el modo seleccionado (el alerón se eleva desde la posición cerrada a la baja carga a 70 km/h, desciende a 50 km/h y pasa a la posición alta carga a 140 km/h). En los modos orientados al rendimiento, como Dinámico, Dinámico+ y Pista, el ala trasera se activa de forma totalmente automática. En las rectas, el sistema cambia a la posición de baja carga para optimizar la velocidad máxima y la estabilidad. El Sistema de Reducción de Resistencia Aerodinámica (DRS), conocido por su uso en la Fórmula 1, se puede activar manualmente (excepto en el modo E-Hybrid) mediante un botón en el volante, permitiendo así alcanzar una velocidad máxima de 351 km/h. Además, el sistema permite elevar automáticamente el ala en curvas a alta velocidad, de modo que la aerodinámica activa contribuya a la eficacia del pilotaje. Durante la frenada y el paso por curva, adopta la posición CA para aumentar la carga aerodinámica y favorecer el control. En esta configuración, el Audi Nuvolari puede generar más de 400 kg de carga aerodinámica a una velocidad de 290 km/h. El Nuvolari combina un chasis de aluminio con paneles externos de CFRP (plástico reforzado con fibra de carbono). Se utilizan procesos de fabricación derivados del automovilismo, como piezas de fibra de carbono preimpregnadas y curadas en autoclave, para lograr la máxima ligereza y rigidez. El Nuvolari también utiliza llantas forjadas con fijación central de un solo perno, algo único en un modelo Audi de producción en serie (aunque heredado del Temerario). Los neumáticos son 255/35 ZR20 delante y 325/30 ZR21 detrás. El sistema de frenado es electrónico (brake-by-wire), por lo que el pedal de freno no tiene conexión física con las ruedas, como sucede en los sistemas hidráulicos convencionales, ya que el proceso se realiza mediante una bomba controlada electrónicamente. Esto facilita la combinación de frenado regenerativo e hidráulico sin variación en la sensación del pedal. Los frenos emplean discos de carbono-cerámicos con un sistema de refrigeración interno que, según los ingenieros alemanes, mejora la disipación del calor en un 21% en comparación con los discos cerámicos de carbono convencionales. Cuenta con pinzas fijas de diez pistones delante y de cuatro detrás. El Audi Nuvolari quattro está equipado con un sistema de "comportamiento predictivo", un ordenador que procesa datos sobre el ángulo de dirección, la aceleración, la velocidad de guiñada y el agarre disponible. Con esta información, el sistema decide cómo distribuir el par motor, la fuerza de frenado y la carga aerodinámica. Hay cinco modos de conducción para elegir: E-Hybrid, para circular en eléctrico por ciudad o en trayectos cortos; Equilibrado (Balanced), para un buen equilibrio entre confort, eficiencia y rendimiento; Dinámico (Dynamic), que ofrece una respuesta más inmediata; Dinámico+ (Dynamic+), que prioriza el rendimiento; y Circuito (Track), el más extremo, con ajustes específicos para pista, incluyendo niveles más tolerantes en el control de tracción. La arquitectura minimalista concentra todos los controles dinámicos esenciales en el volante, para que el conductor pueda centrarse en su misión y sentirse en el centro del mundo. Antes de conducir el Nuvolari, fui copiloto del CEO de Audi, Gernot Döllner, quien me confirmó que esta filosofía minimalista también se hará más visible en los Audi más convencionales en el futuro. "Por supuesto, no llegaremos al extremo del Nuvolari, un hiperdeportivo que prioriza la conducción sobre el rendimiento, pero sí reduciremos el número de pantallas en los Audi del futuro, porque creemos que la impresión orgánica y los controles físicos/analógicos transmiten una imagen más prémium que las pantallas". Es algo similar al contraste entre los relojes analógicos y digitales en el mundo de la relojería. Los asientos ligeros complementan el concepto de interior centrado en el conductor. La estructura de fibra de carbono en la base y en el respaldo reduce el peso, aumenta la rigidez y proporciona una mayor sujeción lateral. Detrás de los asientos se pueden colocar objetos, algo útil porque no hay maletero bajo el capó delantero (debido al S-Duct ya mencionado). El corazón del Nuvolari está formado por cuatro motores que suman 1.001 CV (736 kW) de potencia máxima. El motor V8 biturbo de 4,0 litros genera 800 CV (588 kW), a los que se suman tres motores eléctricos de flujo axial, cada uno con 150 CV (110 kW). Es el mismo sistema de propulsión que se usa en el Lamborghini Temerario, pero allí entrega 920 CV (debido a una calibración de software diferente) y utiliza una batería más pequeña. Es decir, tenemos un Audi que supera al Lamborghini en potencia e incluso en prestaciones: acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,6 segundos frente a los 2,7 del Temerario y alcanza 351 km/h frente a 343 km/h. Dos motores eléctricos se ubican en el eje delantero y el tercero en el trasero, entre el motor V8 central (que alcanza unas increíbles 10.000 rpm, una cifra más común en coches de carreras) y la transmisión automática de doble embrague de ocho velocidades. Los motores delanteros impulsan el Nuvolari y distribuyen el par de forma variable (cifra no revelada por Audi) entre las dos ruedas delanteras, lo que ayuda a definir la trayectoria en las curvas, mejorar la tracción y aumentar la estabilidad. El tercer motor eléctrico (con 300 Nm de par) complementa la entrega de potencia. Este par se utiliza para eliminar el retardo del turbo, suavizar la entrega de potencia del V8 para generar una respuesta más fluida, próxima a la de un motor atmosférico, acelerar los cambios de marcha y activar la función de Launch Control (arranque desde parado sin deslizamiento de las ruedas). Por lo tanto, si el funcionamiento es el mismo que en el Lamborghini, su contribución al par máximo del sistema será de unos 70 Nm (730 del V8 más estos 70 Nm). La propulsión eléctrica añade 201 CV a los 800 del V8 de gasolina (esa es también la potencia disponible cuando el Nuvolari circula exclusivamente en modo eléctrico) para alcanzar los 1.001 CV mencionados anteriormente. Underberg me explica que potencialmente esta contribución podría llegar a 280 CV, pero eso solo serviría para aumentar la potencia máxima durante un breve periodo: "Preferimos una cifra de potencia máxima menor, 1.001 CV, pero este rendimiento es constante y duradero, y la velocidad máxima se puede mantener durante más de cuatro minutos". El sistema híbrido se alimenta de una batería de iones de litio de 7,3 kWh (casi el doble de capacidad que la utilizada en el Lamborghini), instalada donde normalmente se monta el eje de transmisión en un quattro, que no existe en este caso. Su prioridad es suministrar y recuperar energía rápidamente —el Nuvolari puede desacelerar hasta 0,3 g solo mediante regeneración— y no la autonomía eléctrica, que es secundaria, sobre todo porque una batería más grande aumentaría el peso y perjudicaría el rendimiento. No fue una prueba de conducción exhaustiva (eso vendrá después), sino una primera experiencia al volante del Nuvolari, que, según el ingeniero jefe que me acompañaba, representa al 98% el modelo de producción final. Recorrimos unos 10 kilómetros por una carretera sinuosa dentro de una reserva privada en las afueras del pintoresco pueblo de Carmel, cerca del circuito de Laguna Seca, a 180 kilómetros al sur de San Francisco. Me indicaron que no superara los 70 km/h, así que fue una experiencia de conducción preliminar y tranquila. El sonido del V8 es agradable incluso a bajas velocidades, y las aceleraciones iniciales son impresionantes, aunque evidentemente sin poder acercarnos a sus prestaciones máximas. La dirección es más ligera de lo habitual para un hipercoche, y el volante (revestido en Alcántara) también es más fino, dos claras preferencias de Viktor Underberg, como me confesó anteriormente en la presentación de otros deportivos de Audi, especialmente los modelos RS. Pero no por ello es menos precisa y razonablemente directa (2,5 vueltas del volante de tope a tope). Toda mi atención se centró en la pequeña área del panel de instrumentos y en la cara del volante, donde se ubican los cuatro botones que controlan todo lo relacionado con la dinámica: Launch Control modos de conducción, DRS, programas Wet (Mojado), Dry (Seco) y Recharge (Recarga), modo Track (Circuito) y función de elevación hidráulica del morro (dos centímetros). Al pulsarlos rápida o lentamente se activan diferentes funciones y también se pueden girar para acceder a otras configuraciones… pero resulta confuso controlar tantos reglajes de diferentes maneras. Es cierto que un periodista conduce muchos coches a la semana y acaba necesitando tiempo para familiarizarse con el sistema (yo pasé alrededor de una hora en el coche), pero los futuros propietarios del Nuvolari podrían experimentar algo similar. Al fin y al cabo, en sus garajes probablemente tendrán muchos otros coches que alternarán con el Audi más potente y rápido de la historia. Dejé mis críticas constructivas al director ejecutivo de la marca alemana y al director del proyecto, quienes agradecieron los comentarios, pero será difícil que esto cambie dada la filosofía de base del Nuvolari, centrada en mantener siempre la mirada del conductor en la carretera.

articles.title: The Rock-WrestleMania 43 Speculation and WWE Rumors on Drew McIntyre, Charlotte, Alexa Bliss & SNME
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Even though it's expected the Saudi Arabia government will present several WWE legends with lucrative financial offers to be involved in WrestleMania 43 in some capacity, The Rock's film schedule might prevent him from being part of the event.

While speaking with Variety 's Jack Dunn and Marc Malkin , Vin Diesel said the current plan is to start filming Fast Forever , the final movie in the Fast & Furious franchise, in December.

"We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio," Diesel said.

The Rock, who made a cameo appearance in a mid-credits scene at the end of Fast X , is listed in the cast for the new film despite a previous real-life feud with Diesel that played a part in his absence from the eighth and ninth movies.

Steve Carrier of Ringside News noted the filming schedule, particularly for a production of this size, is likely to last months and could stretch into WrestleMania season.

There are variables that could make it so The Rock has a window in his schedule if he wants to be involved at WrestleMania. No one has said the size of his role in the movie, so it's plausible he won't be needed on set for the entire production.

With Saudi Arabia already believed to be paying $250 million to host WrestleMania next year, the expectation is also that the government will present major financial offers to WWE legends to get them on the card in some capacity.

It was previously reported Saudi officials are preparing an offer to The Rock that would be the largest payday ever given to any wrestler to work a single show in the history of the sport.

WWE has dreamed of a Rock-Roman Reigns match for years. The closest it ever got was in 2024 when the Great One appeared on the first Raw of the year to tease a bout with the Tribal Chief that was then scuttled when Cody Rhodes won the Royal Rumble, though The Rock did wrestle on the show in a tag match.

If The Rock is going to do another match, one would assume he would want it to be sooner than later given that he will turn 55 on May 2 and it requires a lot of physical training to keep his body in the shape to be The Rock everyone thinks of in a WWE ring.

WWE Figuring Out Drew McIntyre's Return Storyline

Having been off WWE television since WrestleMania to work on various outside projects, Drew McIntyre is now waiting for creative to find a story to get him back in the ring.

Per PWInsider Elite (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News), McIntyre is back in the United States after completing work on his other commitments, but WWE's creative team hasn't started plotting out his return at this point.

McIntyre lost to Jacob Fatu in an unsanctioned match at WrestleMania 42. The bout was done to write the Scottish Warrior off television for the time being due to being cast in the Highlander reboot and the Russell Crowe-starring The Last Druid .

The Last Druid started filming in Spain in June. Crowe posted a picture with McIntyre on Instagram on Aug. 5, writing they had recently finished filming.

One thing potentially holding up McIntyre's return is all of the people he was feuding with prior to leaving are embroiled in storylines right now. His last two opponents prior to Fatu were Sami Zayn and Cody Rhodes over the undisputed title.

The decision also has to be made if McIntyre will return as a heel or babyface. If he is staying on SmackDown, it might be better to bring him back as a babyface since they just turned Zayn heel and Randy Orton also returned as a villain.

Of course, the Raw roster also needs an infusion of talent, particularly on the heel side. Roman Reigns is the only top level heel—assuming that's what he is supposed to be given his current rivalry with Solo Sikoa and LA Knight—on the Red Brand at this point.

Regardless of what role McIntyre plays when he returns, his presence will be welcome since he had been on one of the best runs of his career prior to taking a leave.

Women's Trios Match Potentially Planned for SNME

With just three matches currently official for the upcoming Sunday Night's Main Event show on Sept. 6, WWE could add a women's trios bout to the card.

Per Joey Votes of WrestleVotes (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), WWE has "loosely discussed" putting Fatal Influence vs. Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley on the SNME show.

"I do know the women's trios match—Fatal Influence vs. Alexa, Tatum, and Charlotte—has been loosely discussed to make that card. They are treating this event as a PLE-lite," JoeyVotes said.

The only matches set for the show are Rhodes vs. Orton, Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker and Baron Corbin vs. Lil Yachty in which Yachty needs to last five minutes to earn Trick Williams a rematch with Corbin for the U.S. title.

WWE has generally put five matches on Saturday Night's Main Event cards, though there have been some exceptions. The Jan. 24 show from Montreal only had three matches take place, though a fourth was scheduled between Rhodes and Fatu that never occurred due to a pre-match brawl.

It would make sense to have the match take place, whether it's on the Sept. 6 card or waiting until Money in the Bank on Oct. 10. Fatal Influence have been feuding with Flair on and off for most of the year. Paxley just recently debuted on SmackDown, so giving her a high-profile match would help elevate her profile.

One thing of note is WWE didn't announce any new matches for SNME during the SmackDown tapings on Monday night for the show airing this week, so the last chance to make it official on the go-home episode on Sept. 4 if it's going to happen.

articles.title: Could Gavin McKenna push Auston Matthews into a new role in the Toronto Maple Leafs NHL lineup
articles.summary: NHL News: With the Toronto Maple Leafs drafting Gavin McKenna first overall, the possibility of reshaping their lineup around him raises intriguing questions about Auston Matthews' role and potential scoring combinations this NHL season.
articles.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs enter the 2026-27 NHL season with the first overall selection in the 2026 NHL Draft, Gavin McKenna, under a microscope. The teenager has yet to play an NHL game, but his arrival is already generating buzz around possible line combinations.Toronto still revolves around Auston Matthews, but the emergence of another top-level offensive talent would give the coaching staff more options. An interesting option would be to have McKenna skate with William Nylander and John Tavares.Could Gavin McKenna join Toronto Maple Leafs top six?Gavin McKenna could be a candidate for a top-six role if he proves in training camp he can handle the speed and physicality of the NHL right away. The Toronto Maple Leafs donât have to push him, but his offensive game could make it harder to decide.William Nylander is entering the season with 79 points, 30 goals and 49 assists in 65 games. At age 35, John Tavares continued to produce, finishing the season with 71 points in 82 games: 31 goals, 40 assists.McKenna joining Nylander and Tavares would give Toronto another potentially potent scoring unit. If the three forwards develop chemistry, it could also pose a tough tactical problem for opposing NHL teams.But that doesnât necessarily mean Auston Matthews would drop in the lineup. Matthews continues to be the leading center for the Toronto Maple Leafs and a huge part of their offensive structure.The training camp and preseason games should be the best barometer for how quickly McKenna can get meaningful NHL minutes. The Toronto coaching staff can see his consistency, defensive responsibility, skating and ability to handle tougher competition before making a decision.A safer bet would be McKenna in a lesser role in the lineup as he adjusts to the NHL. If he adapts quickly, then more responsibility could be on the cards.What would this mean for Auston Matthews?A McKenna breakthrough would provide Jim Hiller with more options in his lineup, notnecessarily take away from the importance of Matthews. Toronto had the ability to spread the scoring out over a number of lines, which may have lessened the burden on one unit to produce the majority of the offence.Right now McKenna's top-six role is still a projection and not a set plan. Still, the possibility is illustrative of the type of buzz surrounding the first overall selection for the Toronto Maple Leafs as the new NHL season approaches.The arrival of Gavin McKenna has prompted new discussion around the Toronto Maple Leafs' forward combinations. The first overall pick could be in line for a top-six role with established scorers William Nylander and John Tavares. If McKenna can make a quick transition, his offensive contributions could give head coach Jim Hiller more flexibility in his lineup next season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
